description:
Hacktoberfest Hack Day Kampala x MUBS is a one-day open source hack day at Makerere University Business School, bringing together students, developers, and first-time contributors from across Kampala to make their first (or fiftieth) pull request together.
Hacktoberfest is a month-long global celebration of open source and this is our contribution to it from MUBS. You don't need to be an advanced programmer to take part. If you have never used Git, never opened a pull request, or have only ever written code for coursework, this event was built with you in mind. We will walk you through the basics from the very beginning: setting up Git and GitHub, finding beginner-friendly issues, forking a repository, making a change, and submitting your first pull request.
What to expect on the day:
A beginner-friendly intro to open source and why it matters for your career
A hands-on walkthrough of Git and GitHub, from zero
Guidance on finding good first issues and projects worth contributing to
Dedicated hacking time with mentors moving around the room to unblock you
Contributions to local and global projects, including ones solving problems in the East African context
Community, snacks, and Hacktoberfest swag
Bring a laptop and a charger. Bring a friend who has been meaning to start coding. That's all you need.
Whether you study Business Computing, Computer Science, design, or something else entirely, there is a way to contribute. Open source needs documentation writers, testers, translators and designers just as much as it needs engineers.
Come and leave with your name on a real project.
#Hacktoberfest

description:
​Hey Pythonistas! Level up your Data & AI game at Hacktoberfest Meetup Quezon City x Python Philippines & RELX. This is a full-day workshop designed to level up your Python skills where we ditch the slides and get straight to coding—covering everything from data wrangling to AI-powered automation.
​Join us on October 3, 2026 at RELX Reed Elsevier, UP Technohub, Quezon City. Whether you're into wrangling data or building AI-powered apps, we've got two parallel tracks lined up just for you:
​Track 1: Data & Analytics
​- Data-Engineered Analytics: Building Schema-Driven Event Pipelines in Python by Alysson Alvaran – Learn how to transform messy, unstructured JSON logs into clean, query-ready tables using Python, Pydantic, and DuckDB.
​- Weather-Weather Lang: What Can Data Tell Us? by Vanessa Althea Bermudez – Explore a practical machine learning workflow using real-world weather data—from data prep to model evaluation.
​Track 2: AI & Automation
​- Generative AI and Prompt Engineering by Lee Mark Chavez – Go beyond basic prompts and learn a structured approach that works at scale, with options for both Python and no-code tracks.
​- Intro to Context Engineering: From Strategic Prompting to Building Apps with Low-Code AI by Daniel Caparro – Learn how to turn strategic prompting into functional applications using low-code and generative AI platforms.
​What to expect:
​- Code-first sessions – This is a workshop, not a lecture. You'll be writing actual Python code throughout the day.
​- Two parallel tracks – Choose the path that fits your interest, whether it's data or AI.
​- Beginner-to-intermediate friendly – Designed for Python users who are ready to take the next step. No prior ML or AI experience required.
​Logistics:
​- What to bring: Laptop with a power cable (we'll provide WiFi and electricity).
​- Food: Snacks and refreshments will be served.
​- Slots: Limited to ensure an optimal hands-on experience for everyone.

description:
Welcome to Hacktoberfest Hack Day Surat 2026!
Join us for an official in-person mini-hackathon held at D2 Seminar Hall (Room 207), CK Pithawala College of Engineering and Technology (CKPCET), supported by Major League Hacking (MLH) and DigitalOcean.
Whether you are a seasoned open-source contributor or a beginner exploring AI, this Hack Day is an energetic building sprint focused on open-source tools, collaborative development, and shipping real projects.
How Team Registration Works:
Strictly Individual Registrations:
MLH requires every participant to have their own individual ticket for check-in verification, safety waivers, and swag accounting.
Forming Your Squad:
Have each of your teammates (solo or teams of 2–4) register using their own email.
Team Finalization:
You will sit together and register your official team name during the on-site check-in session on October 3.
Hackathon Tracks & Themes:
Rather than a rigid single problem statement, this is an open-track sprint. Teams can build any prototype fitting under one of these 3 tracks:
1.
Open-Source AI & Autonomous Agents (Main Track):
Build smart tools, assistants, or autonomous agents using open-weight models (like Google Gemma) or AI APIs.
2.
Developer Tooling & Workflows:
Build practical utilities, CLIs, Git integrations, or developer productivity tools.
3.
Campus & Social Good:
Build solutions addressing student workflow, campus navigation, or community challenges.
Do You Need a PPT?
No pitch decks or PPTs required.
Hackathons are about shipping working software. Judging is based on a
2-minute live demo of your working code
on the projector, paired with a public GitHub repository created during the event.
💻 What to Bring:
Your Laptop & Charger (BYOD):
This is strictly a Bring-Your-Own-Device event.
Active GitHub Account:
To create and push your project repository.
Extension Board (Optional but recommended):
We provide main power strips, but having a compact 2–3 socket extension in your bag is always helpful.
All Attendees:
Exciting developer goodies & official swag, plus refreshments & snacks.

Unlike traditional hackathons that stretch across 24–48 hours, HackOPhobia compresses innovation into just 3 intense hours. Participants must:
Think fast
Build smart
Validate quickly
Deliver a working MVP
Whether it's an AI-powered tool, a productivity app, a web platform, an automation solution, or something completely unexpected — you build it, you pitch it.

A platform to showcase your innovation in front of mentors and evaluators
The Mission:
HackOPhobia is more than just a hackathon — it’s a movement to eliminate the “phobia” of building. Many students hesitate to start because they fear failure, complexity, or judgment.
This event is about:
Taking initiative
Breaking hesitation
Shipping fast
Building with confidence
Because innovation doesn’t wait.

address:

Tampere, Pirkanmaa 33720
Finland
description:
Join us for a one-day hackathon in Tampere where AI engineers, founders, researchers, and curious students come together to build something that matters.
Hosted by TRES and AI Collective in partnership with Hack for Humanity, this event brings Tampere's growing startup scene together with AI community for a single day of fast, hands-on building, with a purpose.
The focus here is exactly what the name says: every problem statement and every project should solve something with the aim of benefiting humanity. Think real problems affecting real people around you, tackled with the AI tools available today.
All types of builders are welcome at this event, whether you're a seasoned engineer or brand new to AI-assisted vibe coding. We'll help solo attendees find a team right at the start, and floating mentors will circulate throughout the day to help with everything from technical architecture to UX and design thinking.
You'll choose from a mix of challenges: some set by our partner companies, some designed by the organizing team, and a few submitted by participants themselves, so there's a problem worth solving for every interest and skill level. Build with whatever tools work for you;
At the end of the day, teams pitch their solutions for a shot at prizes, followed by a Saturday night after-party to celebrate. Sunday is yours to recover. Winning teams may also be invited to showcase their project in Hack for Humanity's global newsletter, reaching 300,000+ subscribers.
Spots are limited, so reserve your place early.
Hack for Humanity: Finland edition
Date: Saturday, 3rd Oct 2026
Time: 09:00 - 21:00
Location: Tampere University Hervanta kampus

description:
AI Collective Skopje is joining Hack for Humanity as part of StartUp Revolution AI Summit.
The AI Collective's global initiative running Fall 2026. It's the continuation of the Humans in AI Week conversations we held this summer, where  we identified real problems in our local community... and now is our chance to build the solutions.
The schedule
15 mins · Problem briefing
3 hours · Hack
45 mins · Demos and judging
The focus here is exactly what the name says. Every problem statement and every project should solve something local to your community, with the purpose of benefiting humanity.
All types of builders are welcome at this event. The winners of this event may be asked to showcase their products within our global newsletter with 300k+ subscribers!

Uses open-source or open-weight AI as an important part of how the project works
Solves a clear problem or creates a useful experience
Shows substantial technical work completed by the team

Has a working demonstration and a clear explanation of what the team built

You'll leave with a simple checklist for picking the right model in minutes, not hours.

description:
Hack for Humanity: Miami
Build what Miami needs next.
Hack for Humanity is The AI Collective's global civic hackathon, running in 120 chapters across 50 countries this fall. Miami's edition is an official MLH Hacktoberfest Hack Day: one day, four challenges, and a room full of builders turning AI into tools our neighbors can use.
Every challenge comes from real problems our community named during Humans in AI Week this summer. All are welcome: developers, designers, data people and anyone who knows a Miami problem up close.
THE FOUR CHALLENGES
01 Four Forces, One City - water, air, land and fire: flooding, hurricanes, housing, extreme heat
02 Wild Miami - animal welfare and protection
03 Brain Gain - helping Miami keep the talent it attracts
04 Data to Action - turning open data into a visual and an action Miami can take
Plus a city partner challenge, announcing soon.
HOW IT WORKS
- Build solo or in teams of up to 4. Looking for teammates? We'll match you at check-in.
- All code is written on the day. Ideas and research beforehand are welcome.
- Submit a public GitHub repo with an open-source license by 3:45 PM.
- Demo live in 2 minutes. Judges score community impact, working build, use of AI and data, originality and demo clarity.
PRIZES
- Grand Champion
- MLH Best Open-Source AI Project: a DEV Badge for every team member
- Hacktoberfest swag for every builder who checks in
- Winners may be invited to join a grant-funded project to commercialize what they built, and showcased in The AI Collective's global newsletter to 450k+ subscribers
WHAT TO BRING
Your laptop, charger, a refillable water bottle and a problem you care about.
Challenge Guide, rules and resources:
https://github.com/AI-Collective-Hackathons/hack-for-humanity-miami
Hosted by The AI Collective, Major League Hacking, The LAB Miami and DeepStation. All participants follow the MLH Code of Conduct:
https://github.com/MLH/mlh-policies/blob/main/code-of-conduct.md

title: [GHW Hacktoberfest] Build with Postgres and AI Agents Using Tiger CLI and MCP
description: Tiger Data (the team behind TimescaleDB) makes Postgres fast for AI and time-series workloads, and its open-source Tiger CLI and MCP server let your AI agent set up and manage a database for you. Justin installs the Tiger CLI, connects the MCP server to an AI coding agent, and uses plain-language prompts to create a service, design a schema, and query data. He also covers how to keep an agent from doing damage, including read-only mode, forking a database to test safely, and other guardrails. You'll leave with a working setup and a safer way to build with AI agents.

title: [GHW Hacktoberfest] Getting Started with Grok Bot & Cursor
description:
Ready to level up your developer workflow? Join Fiona Whittington from SpaceXAI to learn how you can build software and solve your problems faster than ever.
Fiona will show you how you can pair the AI-powered capabilities of Cursor with the orchestration power of Grok Bot to build an entire internship stack from scratch.
Along the way, we'll break down the basics of agentic coding. You’ll learn how to move past simple copy-pasting and treat AI like a reliable coding partner, one that can help you plan features, write code across multiple files, and hunt down stubborn bugs in seconds.
Whether you’re hunting for your first tech role or just want to ship personal projects without getting stuck, this workshop will give you practical tools you can start using today.
Don't forget to sign up for Cursor Pro! Check your pre-event email for more details.

Shastra Spark is a Hacktoberfest 2026 Hack Day hosted by TCET Shastra Club at Thakur College of Engineering & Technology, Mumbai.
This year, under the theme “Craft The Future”, participants will get the opportunity to move beyond ideas and build practical solutions to real-world problems using open-source AI, open-weight models and modern developer tools.

address:

description:
Presented by NIT Hamirpur Chapter : GDG Ludhiana in partnership with Major League Hacking (MLH).
About the Event
Get ready to innovate, build, and connect! Hacktoberfest Hack day Hamirpur x GDG Ludhiana is a high-energy, one-day in-person mini hackathon hosted at NIT Hamirpur as part of Hacktoberfest, the world's largest celebration of open source.
This year's theme centers on open source and open-weight AI: models, tools, and agents that anyone can inspect, run, and build upon. It's a fast-paced collaborative day where you arrive in the morning, form a team, build a small, real-world project from scratch, and demo it that same afternoon.
Welcoming Freshers & Curious Minds!
A huge welcome to all freshers, first-year students, and complete beginners: you do NOT need to be a seasoned coder or have a background in AI to participate!
Whether you write code, design user interfaces, or are simply curious about open-source technology and how things work, there is a seat at the table for you. All you need to bring is your curiosity, enthusiasm, and a willingness to learn in an inclusive, safe, and judgment-free environment.
What’s In It For You?
1. Prizes, Swag & Goodies: Inclusive tracks tailored for everyone,whether you are a complete beginner, an experienced coder, or someone who just wants to explore technology and build something fun.
2. Community Interaction & Tech Talks: Gain insightful knowledge through interactive workshops, expert-led talks, and peer sessions that break down open-source, developer tools, and modern AI.
3. Hands-on Mentorship & Portfolio Growth: Work side-by-side with experienced mentors who will help turn your ideas into a real, published GitHub repository, boosting your developer portfolio in just one day.
Who Can Attend?
1.Freshers & First-Time Contributors: Curiosity is the only prerequisite. We need no prior open-source experience needed!
2. Students, Developers, & Designers: From beginners writing their first lines of code to experienced builders pushing their limits.
3. Tech Enthusiasts: Anyone eager to collaborate, connect with peers, and experience real hackathon culture.
What You Will Do :
1. Form a Team & Build: Create a working project from scratch on the day using open-source tools or open-weight AI models.
2. Share Your Work: Push your project to a public GitHub repository under an open-source license.
3. Demo Your Project: Present a quick 5-minute live demo of what your team built.
Important Rule
All development work must start at the event. Projects or codebases begun before the day are strictly not eligible. Come with fresh ideas, enthusiasm, and curiosity not pre-existing code!

This is a new theme, so be on the lookout for more info as we get closer.
Global Hack Week takes place throughout the year to give you a chance to complete technical challenges, network with the community, enjoy fun live sessions, build technical projects, and make new memories.
Livestreams and Mini Events
Throughout GHW, we'll have daily workshops live-streamed on our Twitch to give you the chance to pick up new skills and build something together with the community. In between workshops, we'll run mini-events in the MLH Community Discord for you to join in and meet friends as you take a break from hacking.
Challenges and Points
At GHW: Hacktoberfest we will have plenty of challenges to keep you busy. Challenges will range from social challenges urging you to connect with other members of the community, technical challenges that will expand your coding skills, and design challenges to refine your skills as a creator and artist. Some of these challenges will be completed live on our twitch stream, so you can follow along and complete it with the community. We cannot wait to see all that you learn, build, and share.
Earn experience points for yourself by completing our challenges throughout GHW. Challenges aren’t the only way to earn points. You can also receive a point each time you check in for a live session, so the more you attend, the more points you’ll rack up. They can be as simple as posting on your social media or as advanced as building a project and creating a full demo video for it. We’ll leave it to you to choose which challenges you want to take on. Feel free to work collaboratively with others on these.

address:

One97 Communications Ltd. Unit No. 3 & 4A, 3rd Floor

description:
Join us for Hacktoberfest 2026 in Mumbai — a community-driven day dedicated to open-source AI, collaboration, and building in public. 🚀
This year's theme is AI BELONGS TO EVERYONE 🤖. You'll spend the day learning, experimenting, and shipping with open-source and open-weight AI models — solo or in a team. Whether you're a first-time contributor or an experienced open-source developer, come together with fellow hackers to learn, contribute, collaborate, and get your pull requests merged.
⚠️ IMPORTANT: Luma registration is mandatory. Registering on this page alone is not enough — you must also register at
https://luma.com/rtta1cub
. Only approved Luma participants will be allowed to attend.
📅 11 October 2026
⏰ 9:00 AM – 5:00 PM
📍 Paytm – One 97 Communications Ltd, Mumbai
Challenges 🏆
Best Use of Gemma 4
It's time to see how much you can build with a lightweight, open model. Gemma 4 packs multimodal intelligence into an open-weights model that you can access through the Gemini API. So, what can Gemma 4 bring to your project?
Multimodal Experience: Work with text and images to create an assistant that understands more of what users share.
Focused AI Tools: Build a focused AI tool for learning, creativity, productivity, or your community.
Rapid Prototyping: Experiment with an open model while using the Gemini API to move quickly from an idea to a working prototype.
Bring your idea to life… what will you build with Gemma 4 today?
Best Open-Source AI Project
Build an original project that uses open-source or open-weight AI as an important part of how it works. Teams could create an agent skill, build with an open-weight large or small language model, or build or adapt an open-source model harness. These are examples within one challenge, and teams may combine them.
Open-source or open-weight AI must be an important part of the project.
The project must be published in a public GitHub repository and use an open-source license.
An agent skill must comply with the Agent Skill Open Standard.
A model-harness entry must include an original implementation or meaningful changes to an existing open-source harness.
What to expect
🧑‍💻 Work on real open-source AI projects and submit contributions
🤝 Meet and collaborate with developers from the community
🛠️ Learn how to contribute through Git and GitHub
💡 Discover new projects, tools, and ideas
🌐 Connect with fellow open-source enthusiasts
🔥 Spend the day hacking, learning, and shipping
Bring your laptop, your ideas, and your willingness to build. Whether it's your first pull request or your fiftieth, there's a place for you.
Let's hack, contribute, and celebrate open source together!

description:
Ducktoberfest is Orduck Community's first hackathon, organized in partnership with Hacktoberfest, and we're building it around one simple idea: give developers and AI enthusiasts in Baku a full day to actually build something with open-source AI, rather than just talk about it.
Over the course of the day, teams of 3 will pick a challenge, design a solution, and build a working AI agent or automation project using open-source models and tools. By the end of the event, each team presents their project to a panel of judges, who'll evaluate what was built and select the standout teams. Whether you're already deep into open source or just curious about AI agents, this event is built for hands-on learners who want to spend the day actually shipping something.
The Challenge
Build a project centered on an AI agent or automation workflow using open-source or open-weight models and tools. This could mean creating an agent skill, building on top of an existing open-source model, or adapting an existing open-source project into something new. Teams are free to combine approaches.

🕘

09:00 to 17:00
📍

Peerstack Academy, Azerbaijan Technical University, Baku
👥

Hacktoberfest merch and prizes for participants, feedback from our judging panel, and a full day working alongside other builders.

title: Hacktoberfest Hack Day Hyderabad x NIAT - KKH
address:
No. 144, Survey No. 37
5th, Kapil Kavuri Hub, Financial District, Nanakramguda
Hyderabad, Telangana 500032
India
description:
Hacktoberfest 2026 — Student Open Source Hack Day
Let's gather for a student-focused open-source hacking experience where students can learn, build, collaborate, and make meaningful contributions to real-world projects.
Whether you're making your first open-source contribution or already familiar with GitHub, this event is an opportunity to learn by doing, connect with fellow student developers, and experience the open-source community.
Students can participate individually or form small teams based on their interests and skills, work on open-source projects, and receive guidance throughout the event.
Event Structure & Agenda
Kickoff & Hacktoberfest Briefing
Welcome students, introduce Hacktoberfest and the fundamentals of open-source contribution, and explain how students can participate. Share project repositories, contribution guidelines, GitHub resources, and useful learning materials.
Idea Sharing & Team Formation
Students share project or contribution ideas, discuss areas they're interested in, ask questions, and form teams based on complementary skills and interests. Students who prefer to work independently can also choose their own open-source project.
Hacking & Mentorship Session
Students spend dedicated time exploring repositories, understanding codebases, fixing bugs, improving documentation, adding features, and creating pull/merge requests. Mentors and experienced student contributors provide guidance on Git, GitHub, code reviews, debugging, and contribution best practices.
Student Demos & Showcase
Students showcase what they built or contributed during the event. Each participant or team can give a short demo highlighting their contribution, the problem they worked on, what they learned, and the pull/merge request they submitted.
Wrap-Up & Student Networking
Celebrate student contributions and participation, share key learnings, and recognize notable projects and contributions. Students can connect with other developers, exchange ideas, discover new open-source projects, and find opportunities to continue contributing together.
Come learn, build, contribute, and grow with open source!
Happy hacking! 🚀

description:
Curious about how AI can make your life easier as a student, hacker, and future software engineer? Join Dina Blachman for an introduction Cursor and Grok Bot.

Rather than just looking at theoretical code, you’ll get to see real-world, practical workflows built specifically for students, from streamlining class projects and personal hacks to supercharging your internship hunt and recruiting prep.
Whether you're completely new to AI-assisted coding or looking for smart ways to work faster during hackathons, this session will show you how to start using Cursor and Grok Bot right away.

description:
Come spend an evening hacking on real hardware and open-source AI with the Indy dev community. We’ve filled a room with gear you probably don’t have on your desk at home. Pick something that looks fun and start building.
Whether this is your first open-source contribution or your fiftieth, there’s a place for you here. No hardware or AI experience needed.
What to expect
- Arduino Uno Q boards to hack on. The Uno Q pairs a Linux computer with a microcontroller on a single board, with 4 GB of RAM and 32 GB of storage. Its built-in LED matrix lets you get something on screen within minutes. We’ll have a demo unit running, starter examples to try, and monitors and USB-C docks if you want to plug in.
- Meet Reachy Mini. Our small open-source robot runs on a fully local AI stack, with no cloud involved. Stop by and say hi, and it will greet you back.
- Run models on a local GPU. Bring a laptop and connect to our eGPU to run open-weight models on your own hardware.
- Access to Qwen models. Thanks to the LLM Collective, we’ll provide a temporary shared API key so you can build with open-weight Qwen models during the event.
- Open-source contributions, community, and swag.
- Food!
What to bring
Your laptop, a charger, a GitHub account, and your curiosity.

description:
HACKTOBERFEST: FALL 2026
​The Atlanta chapter is joining Hack for Humanity, The AI Collective's global initiative running Fall 2026. It's the continuation of the Humans in AI Week conversations we held this summer, where we identified real problems in our local community... and now is our chance to build the solutions. This hackathon is being supported by Major League Hacking (MLH).
Join us Tuesday, October 14 at Improving in Alpharetta for a hack to help parents with children age 7-17 learn how to safely interact with AI.
​The focus here is exactly what the name says. Every problem statement and every project should solve something local to our community, with the purpose of benefiting humanity.
​While all types of builders are welcome at this event, we encourage parents of children age 7-17 & young adults to participate. Participants must be 18+ to submit a product. The winners of this event may be asked to showcase their products within our global newsletter with 300k+ subscribers!
​RSVP and we'll see you there.
​Please be advised: Unfortunately, space is very limited at these community events and we can not always accept everyone we would like to. If you are not accepted to this event, please keep applying! We appreciate your application tremendously and we are looking forward to seeing you at a future event very soon!
​The AI Collective is a global non-profit building the human layer for the AI era. We unite 300,000+ leaders, builders, and stakeholders across 250+ forums worldwide to democratize the frontier, build trust, and coordinate how society navigates the rapid acceleration of technological progress.
​All attendees and organizers at events affiliated with The AI Collective agree to our privacy policy and are subject to our code of conduct.

title: Hacktoberfest Meetup Melbourne x Melbourne GitHub User Group
address:
Level 5, 440 Collins Street
Melbourne, VIC 3000
Australia
description:
This is your Hacktoberfest Meetup Melbourne edition! We're super excited to host this in Australia, and hope you can all come along.
Join us for a night of mingling with other developers, hear about GitHub, open-source, and open-weight, and get excited for all the amazing things happening around AI assisted coding. You'll hear talks and content from people who are building and using open-source AI models and open-weight AI models.
Food will be provided, and there will be SWAG (door prizes with GitHub merch, SWAG from our sponsors, and special Hacktoberfest goodies), so get excited!
Thank you to our generous venue sponsor: Arinco, and our food and drinks sponsor Twilio.
Talk details:
Talk 1:
Roll for Recap: Turning Session Chaos into Agent Powered Summaries by AJ Bajada
In Roll for Recap, AJ walks through how vibe coding can bring a brand new feature to life for tabletop play. This time the focus is a Session Notes and Recap Engine that takes messy player notes, structures them, and transforms them into clear and entertaining summaries using skills.md and open weight models. No prophecy from the DM, no ancient architecture scrolls, just curiosity, instinct, and a willingness to let the notes and the agent fall where they may.
AJ shows how raw session notes can become tactical recaps, narrative recaps, humorous recaps, and even radio show style summaries. Along the way you will see how skills.md shapes agent behaviour and how open weight models help the system stay consistent, expressive, and grounded in the rules and lore of the game.
It is a real example of how vibe coding, when done with intention instead of chaotic neutral energy, can build useful agent features and bring a tabletop world to life with surprising speed and style.
Talk 2:
Local AI: Twenty Gigabytes and suspicious amount of confidence by Dennis Vroegop
Somebody on your team has downloaded 20 gigabytes from Hugging Face and announced that you're now doing open-source AI. Nobody has read the licence. But it runs on a laptop, so apparently security is sorted too.
A remarkable amount of confidence to extract from a progress bar.
In this 45-minute session, we'll run models live on a laptop: no cloud, no API key, and no screenshot of something that worked last week. We'll cover what you've actually downloaded, why open weights aren't automatically open source, which models deserve your disk space, and what hardware you need. We'll also look honestly at speed, quality and cost.
Then we'll tackle what "local" doesn't solve. A wrong answer doesn't become right because you paid for the electricity. And keeping data on your machine is a useful guarantee, not your entire security strategy.
You'll leave knowing how to get useful results locally and when to choose local over cloud. With numbers and a working example. Which is a nice change from the unshakeable conviction of someone who has watched half a tutorial.

is a casual, discussion-style Hacktoberfest meetup at Dharmsinh Desai University, Nadiad, for students of every year and department, with a special focus on first-years.
Most students find out about open-source AI, developer communities and hackathons in their third or fourth year, long after the best chances to benefit from them. This session is about getting there earlier.

Part 1, Open source and AI, an introduction:
what open source is, how licenses work, where it all came from, and how it connects to modern AI

Part 2, Running open-source AI models on your own laptop:
how to pick a model that fits your hardware and use case, and run it locally with Ollama, with no cloud and no subscription

a hands-on walkthrough of setting it up with NVIDIA NIM APIs, to code with a much larger model than your laptop can run

description:
Hack for Humanity Carmen–Campeche
es un hackatón intensivo de un día: llegas por la mañana, formas equipo y sales por la tarde con un prototipo funcional que ataca una problemática local de Ciudad del Carmen y de la región.
El reto no es solo programar, es identificar un problema real de tu comunidad —movilidad, medio ambiente, salud, educación, servicios públicos, economía local— y demostrar una solución viable en menos de seis horas. Para lograrlo en ese tiempo, el uso de inteligencia artificial no es opcional: queremos que la IA sea tu copiloto durante todo el día, desde la exploración de la idea hasta la generación de código y la preparación del pitch.
Los equipos
Los equipos se forman
el mismo día del evento
, así que no necesitas llegar con uno armado, aunque si puedes tener un acuerdo previo. Si vienes solo, te ayudamos a integrarte. Serán de
máximo 5 integrantes
, conformados por estudiantes de nivel superior, y damos preferencia a los equipos
multidisciplinarios
: programación, diseño, comunicación, negocios, ciencias naturales, ciencias de la salud, ingeniería y ciencias sociales resuelven mejor juntos que por separado. Cada equipo contará con un docente asesor (si no tienen un previamente acordado, se les asignará el día del evento). También contaremos con la participación de mentores que aportarán su experiencia a todos los equipos.
Nota: Cupo límitado. Se dará preferencia conforme al orden de registro.
Las presentaciones
Cada equipo tendrá
5 minutos máximo
para presentar su prototipo ante el jurado. Cuida el tiempo: un pitch breve y claro vale más que una demo larga que no se entiende.
Premiación
Los premios son cortesía de MLH y de los patrocinadores asignados. Se premiará al primer lugar de los retos del evento, premios adicionales sujetos a disponibilidad.
Registro y Check-in
El registro esta abierto desde el Lunes 17 de Agosto 2026. Cabe señalar que para hacer efectiva la participación, deberá realizarse en esta plataforma un Check-in el día del evento, con el fin de corroborar que efectivamente quien se pre-inscribio está participando.
Constancias de Participación
Después de registrarte y hacer check in el día del evento, estarán disponibles para su descarga directamente en esta plataforma (MLH) en formato digital.
Snacks
Los participantes que se preinscriban, y al asistir al evento hagan check-in en MLH, serán considerados para recibir su bebida y snacks durante la ejecución del evento.
¿Qué es GitHub?
GitHub es la plataforma donde vive el software del mundo. Más de cien millones de desarrolladores la usan para guardar su código, llevar el historial de cada cambio y trabajar en equipo sin pisarse el trabajo unos a otros. Cada proyecto vive en un
repositorio
: una carpeta con superpoderes que registra quién hizo qué, cuándo y por qué, y que permite volver atrás cuando algo se rompe.
Para un hackatón es la herramienta natural: tu equipo trabaja en paralelo sobre el mismo proyecto, el repositorio queda como evidencia pública de lo que construyeron, y ese enlace se vuelve parte de tu portafolio profesional.
GitHub es patrocinador de este evento
, y el uso de GitHub y GitHub Copilot forma parte de la rúbrica de evaluación. Sube tu proyecto a un repositorio desde el arranque y documenta el proceso.
¿Qué es GitHub Copilot?
GitHub Copilot es el asistente de programación con IA integrado en GitHub y en editores como Visual Studio Code. Sugiere líneas y funciones completas mientras escribes, explica código que no conoces, propone correcciones a errores y permite conversar con tu propio proyecto para entenderlo o modificarlo. En un hackatón de seis horas, es la diferencia entre una idea contada y una idea demostrada.
Copilot es
gratuito para estudiantes verificados
a través del GitHub Student Developer Pack.
Requisitos
Trae tu propio equipo de cómputo
(y no olvides el cargador). Recomendamos traer extensiones.
Check-in
: Hacer check-in el día del evento, lo haces desde tu cuenta de la plataforma de MLH. Si tienes problemas con esta parte puedes preguntar al staff el día del evento.
Entregar proyecto
en la plataforma de MLH, con repositorio de GitHub. Solo uno de los miembros del equipo entrega.

Evento desarrollado por el
Capítulo Campeche de The AI Collective
en colaboración con la
Universidad Autónoma del Carmen
, siguiendo los lineamientos de
Hacktoberfest
de
Major League Hacking (MLH)
, en el marco de la iniciativa
Hack for Humanity
de The AI Collective.

description:
Spend a week hacking with the MLH community at Global Hack Week: Hacktoberfest! Global Hack Week takes place throughout the year to give you a chance to complete technical challenges, network with the community, enjoy fun live sessions, build technical projects, and make new memories.
This is a new theme, so be on the lookout for more info as we get closer.
Global Hack Week takes place throughout the year to give you a chance to complete technical challenges, network with the community, enjoy fun live sessions, build technical projects, and make new memories.
Livestreams and Mini Events
Throughout GHW, we'll have daily workshops live-streamed on our Twitch to give you the chance to pick up new skills and build something together with the community. In between workshops, we'll run mini-events in the MLH Community Discord for you to join in and meet friends as you take a break from hacking.
Challenges and Points
At GHW: Hacktoberfest we will have plenty of challenges to keep you busy. Challenges will range from social challenges urging you to connect with other members of the community, technical challenges that will expand your coding skills, and design challenges to refine your skills as a creator and artist. Some of these challenges will be completed live on our twitch stream, so you can follow along and complete it with the community. We cannot wait to see all that you learn, build, and share.

title: Hacktoberfest Hack Day Taipei x The AI Collective Taipei Chapter
address:
Section 2, Wuchang St, 83之6號3樓
Taipei City,  Wanhua District 108
Taiwan
description:
Build for the people and places around you
​On October 17, The AI Collective Taipei is joining Hack for Humanity, a global initiative that brings communities together to build technology for real human needs. For this Taiwan chapter, we’ll focus on local challenges that affect everyday life. From supporting families and caregivers to navigating disasters and protecting the information ecosystem, with the operational help of Major League Hacking, we’ll spend the day turning local problems into practical prototypes.
​Whether you’re a developer, designer, researcher, domain expert, student, founder, or simply someone who cares about Taiwan’s future, you’re invited to build with us. You don’t need to arrive with a team or a fully formed idea, we’ll help you find collaborators and a problem worth solving.
​The goal is not to build a perfect product in one day. It’s to understand a meaningful problem, create something useful, and leave with a prototype that can continue growing.
​Taiwan’s four challenges tracks
​Reversing the Birthrate Decline
​Family Support Systems Taiwan has one of the lowest fertility rates in the world. For many families, the challenge is not simply whether to have children—it’s whether life with children feels manageable. Parents often struggle to find reliable information about childcare subsidies, locate available public preschools, and balance work, caregiving, and family life. How might we make family support easier to discover, understand, and access?
​Potential data sources:
​Ministry of the Interior population and household statistics
​Ministry of Education preschool locations and vacancy data
​Ministry of Health and Welfare childcare subsidy open data
​2. Tech for a Super-Aged Society
​Long-Term Care Taiwan is entering a super-aged society, with more than 20% of the population expected to be aged 65 or older by 2026. Caregivers are under increasing pressure, while many older adults face isolation, mobility challenges, and difficulty navigating long-term care services. How might technology help older adults live with greater independence—and help caregivers feel less alone?
​Potential data sources:
​Ministry of Health and Welfare Long-Term Care 2.0 service data
​Ministry of the Interior aging index maps
​Taiwan National Health Insurance open statistics
​3. Civic Tech & Fighting Misinformation
​Cognitive Resilience Taiwan’s information environment is fast-moving and increasingly complex. Misinformation spreads daily through LINE, social media, and online communities, affecting public trust and civic life. How might we help people assess information, understand public issues, and participate more confidently in society?
​Potential data sources:
​Cofacts（真的假的）open API
​Central Election Commission voting and turnout data
​g0v civic datasets
​4. Climate & Disaster Resilience
​Typhoons, Floods & Earthquakes
​Taiwan is highly exposed to typhoons, torrential rain, flooding, and earthquakes. During a crisis, timely and understandable information can save lives. How might we help people prepare before disasters happen and make better decisions when they do?
​Potential data sources:
​Central Weather Administration APIs
​Water Resources Agency flood sensors
​National Science and Technology Center for Disaster Reduction warning feeds
​Build with Lovable
​Lovable is the official Taiwan partner for this hackathon. Participants will receive Lovable credits to help turn their ideas into working prototypes quickly. Whether you’re an experienced developer or building your first product, Lovable gives teams a way to move from concept to usable interface and testable idea in a short amount of time. Bring a problem you care about. We’ll help you build a first version.
​Who should join?
​Developers and software engineers
​Designers and product thinkers
​Data scientists and researchers
​Students and first-time hackers
​Civic innovators and social entrepreneurs
​People working in healthcare, education, climate, public policy, or community services
​You can participate as an individual or join a team on the day. All experience levels are welcome.
​Event details
​Date: Saturday, October 17, 2026
​Time: 12pm to 7pm
​Location: collaplay, Ximen, Taipei
​Organizers: The AI Collective Taipei × Major League Hacking Official Taiwan partner: Lovable
​Cost: Free
​Language: English & Mandarin
​Please bring a charged laptop. More details will be announced soon.
​About Hack for Humanity
​Hack for Humanity is a global initiative by The AI Collective focused on building technology that addresses real challenges in local communities. Every city brings its own context, needs, and perspective. By building locally and sharing globally, we can create solutions that are grounded in real life—and contribute to a more human-centered future for technology. Join us in Taipei and help build something that matters.
​Please be advised: Unfortunately, space is very limited at these community events and we can not always accept everyone we would like to. If you are not accepted to this event, please keep applying! We appreciate your application tremendously and we are looking forward to seeing you at a future event very soon!

description:
⚠️ Important: Registration on MLH OrganizerHQ does not guarantee attendance. All applicants must complete the Hackerspace Mumbai application on Luma
https://luma.com/hlu6x87w
. Final attendance decisions are communicated through Luma.​
AI belongs to everyone. This October, Hacktoberfest enters a bold new chapter. The days of chasing arbitrary pull-request counts are in the past; this year, we’re coming together for a high-impact, in-person Hack Day focused on hands-on building, experimenting, and shipping with open-source AI and open-weight models.
​Organized by Hackerspace Mumbai in collaboration with our Ecosystem Partner, Paytm, this one-day fest gathers Mumbai’s developers, students, researchers, and builders to explore the frontier of open AI tooling.
​What We’re Hacking On
​Instead of small PR tweaks, this Hack Day is all about practical, builder-first collaboration:
​Open-Source AI Agents: Orchestrating multi-agent systems, autonomous workflows, and agent evaluation.
​Open-Weight & Local Models: Running, benchmarking, and fine-tuning models locally using Ollama, vLLM, and Hugging Face.
​Modern Developer Protocols: Implementing tool-use, skills.md, Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, and secure agent identities.
​Full-Stack AI Apps: Building practical RAG pipelines and integrating open AI models into everyday web, mobile, and backend apps.
​Who Should Attend?
​Whether you run models on dedicated local GPUs or call APIs from lightweight notebooks, there is a table for you:
​Solo Hackers & Project Leads: Bring an open-source repo, prototype an agentic idea, or build out an open-weight tool.
​Collaborators & First-Time AI Builders: Team up with other builders on sprint challenges, scaffold tools, and learn modern open-source AI workflows hands-on.
​Mentors & Maintainers: Facilitate project tables, guide peers through model runtimes, and review architectures.

address:

Milano, Milano 20154
Italy
description:
One day to build, experiment, and contribute to open source.
For Hacktoberfest, Coding Bunker is changing its format: no event based only on talks and slides, but a
hands-on Hack Day
dedicated to building projects with
open-source technologies, open-source AI, and open-weight models
.
The goal is simple: bring together developers, QA engineers, DevOps engineers, architects, designers, and technology enthusiasts to
form teams, turn an idea into something that works, and learn by building together
.
You do not need to arrive with a ready-made project. In fact, according to the official Hacktoberfest Hack Day rules,
work on the submitted project must begin during the event
.
How it will work
During the Hack Day:
Team formation
: you can join other participants, find a team directly at the event, or work on your own idea
Ideation
: choose a real problem to solve and define your project
Build
: you will have several hours to design, develop, test, and improve your solution
Open Source AI
: projects will use open-source technologies and/or open-weight AI models
Mentoring and collaboration
: throughout the day, you will be able to exchange ideas with other participants and share approaches, problems, and solutions
Project submission
: at the end of the Hack Day, teams will submit their projects through the official OrganizerHQ Challenges platform
Demo and judging
: we will close the day by showcasing what has been built and evaluating the participating projects
We are not necessarily looking for the most complex project.
We are looking for
interesting ideas, experimentation, collaboration, and something that actually works by the end of the day
.
Hacktoberfest Challenges
Coding Bunker is taking part in the official
Major League Hacking Hacktoberfest Hack Day
format.
During the event, one or more
official Hacktoberfest open-source prize challenges
may be available, together with any partner challenges assigned to the event.
Details about the challenges and any associated prizes will be shared with participants before or during the Hack Day.
Hacktoberfest swag and digital badges
will also be available according to the terms of the official program.
Who can participate?
It does not matter whether you are a:
developer
QA / Quality Engineer
DevOps / Platform Engineer
architect
data or AI engineer
designer
open-source contributor
or simply curious and eager to experiment
You do not need to be an AI expert or a regular open-source contributor.
The Hack Day is also designed as an opportunity to learn, experiment with new technologies, and work with people whose skills are different from your own.
Bring your laptop, your desire to build, and a few ideas.
We will figure out the rest together.
Registration
As required by the official Hacktoberfest guidelines,
participant registration and check-in will be managed through OrganizerHQ
.
We will share the official registration link as soon as it becomes available.
What is Hacktoberfest?
Hacktoberfest is an international initiative focused on growth and collaboration within the open-source ecosystem.
In 2026, Hacktoberfest events focus on the opportunity to
learn, experiment, and build using open-source technologies and open-weight AI
.
The Coding Bunker Hack Day is part of the
Hacktoberfest Hack Day
format, an in-person event dedicated to building projects through a mini-hackathon approach.
Coding Bunker
Coding Bunker is a community dedicated to Software Engineering and to sharing real-world experiences among professionals.
Testing, Architecture, AI, DevOps, Cloud, Observability, Performance, Accessibility, and Software Craftsmanship are just some of the topics we cover.
This time, though, instead of just talking about them...
let's build something together.
Telegram Link
https://t.me/codingbunker
Legal Notice
By participating in the event, attendees authorize the organizers to take photographs and video recordings and to use the collected material for communication, promotional, and documentation purposes related to Coding Bunker, Hacktoberfest, and the community.

title: Hacktoberfest Hack Day Boca Raton (FAU) x The AI Collective
address:

United States
description:
Hack for Humanity — FAU. Teams of 2–4. Improve one small corner of the world for humanity.
A patient's covered claim gets denied and she never appeals — not because she'd lose, but because appealing costs more than the claim is worth. A child's IEP promises 90 minutes of therapy a week, and whether she got it lives on paper sign-in sheets nobody reconciles until the annual review. No rule was broken in either story. What failed was legibility: nobody could see the whole picture at once, so it had to be rebuilt by hand, by the person least able to spare the time.
You'll pick one of the challenges — real published requirements written out as structured data with a citation on every rule, plus a synthetic document set messy enough to be honest:
A · Return to Play — proving concussion protocol steps actually happened B · Campus Safety Report — Clery reporting assembled by hand from six offices C · Care Denied — the appeal nobody has hours to file D · Services Owed — IEP service minutes promised vs. delivered E · Grant Integrity — proving funded money was spent the way the award said
Five rules: cite everything, never make the final call, synthetic data only, rules are data not code, fail toward caution.
No experience required. The teams that win these are almost never the most technically advanced — they're the ones who picked something small, finished it, and could say in one sentence why it mattered. Starter repo, packs, mentors, food, and judges from the offices that actually own these problems all provided.

description:
KrowdKraft Community is hosting
Hacktoberfest Hack Day Bengaluru 2026
, a free, in-person Hack Day bringing together developers, students, professionals, open-source contributors and builders for a full day of learning, collaboration and building.
The Hack Day is part of Hacktoberfest 2026 and will focus on
open-source AI and hands-on project building
.
Whether you're an experienced developer or exploring open source for the first time, you're welcome to participate.
Prize tracks
Best Open-Source AI Project
Build an original project that uses open-source or open-weight AI as an important part of how it works. Teams could create an agent skill, build with an open-weight large or small language model, or build or adapt an open-source model harness. description:
Hacktoberfest Hack Day Gwalior × ABV-IIITM IEEE
Build with Open Source AI. Learn by Doing. Create Something Meaningful.
Get ready to turn your ideas into reality at
Hacktoberfest Hack Day Gwalior × ABV-IIITM IEEE
, an in-person mini-hackathon hosted by the IEEE Student Branch at ABV-IIITM Gwalior as part of
Hacktoberfest 2026
, powered by Major League Hacking (MLH) and DEV in partnership with DigitalOcean.
Read this before registering
This year's Hacktoberfest theme is
“AI Belongs to Everyone”
, with a focus on exploring open-source AI tools and open-weight models. The goal is to make AI more accessible by encouraging developers, students, and curious minds to experiment with these technologies, learn from one another, and build practical solutions.
Whether you're a beginner taking your first steps into AI and open source or an experienced developer ready to experiment with new ideas, this is your opportunity to collaborate, learn, and build. Work individually or team up with fellow builders to develop a project, explore open-source AI, and showcase what you create by the end of the Hack Day.
Expect a day filled with hands-on building, creative problem-solving, peer learning, and meaningful collaboration with the developer community. You don't need a groundbreaking idea to get started; bring your curiosity, your laptop, and the willingness to build something new.
What to expect:
- A hands-on mini-hackathon centred around open-source AI.
- An opportunity to experiment with open-source AI tools and open-weight models.
- Collaborative project building, experimentation, and final demos.
- A chance to connect with fellow students, developers, and open-source enthusiasts.
- In-kind prizes and goodies for selected participants or winning teams, subject to availability.
A few things to know:
This is a limited-capacity, in-person event. Submitting the interest form does not guarantee participation. Confirmed participants and waitlisted applicants will be notified separately. All prizes will be in kind; no cash awards will be offered.
Come with an idea, leave with a project, and be part of a community that believes the future of AI should be open, accessible, and built together.

title: Hacktoberfest Hack Day Bengaluru x OLake
address:
HustleHub H203, 522, 
24th Main Rd, Parangi Palaya, Sector 2, HSR Layout, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560102
BENGALURU, Karnataka 560102
India
description:
Hacktoberfest Hack Day Bengaluru x OLake
is a one-day, in-person hackathon at the OLake office in HSR Layout, focused on open-source AI.
OLake
is an open-source data platform with two parts:
OLake ingestion
copies data from databases and streams (Postgres, MySQL, MongoDB, Oracle, MSSQL, DB2, Kafka, S3) into Apache Iceberg or Parquet.
OLake Fusion
keeps those Iceberg tables healthy with automated maintenance such as compaction.
This year there is only one path that you can pick and build solo:
##
Ask OLake:
a chat assistant for the OLake docs
Build a chat assistant for the
OLake docs
that answers user questions about both: setup, source configuration, sync modes, catalogs, table maintenance, deployment and troubleshooting.
Use the OLake docs and the open-source repos (olake, olake-ui, olake-helm, olake-fusion). Bring in outside sources when the docs aren't enough. Every answer must cite its sources and say clearly when it doesn't know.
It will run on a public website, so build it as if it's going to production.
What to submit (by 6:30 PM)
A publicly reachable endpoint:
POST /ask
with
{"question": "..."}
returning
{"answer": "...", "sources": ["<url>", ...]}
A chat UI that can be embedded in a docs site
Your repo, with a README explaining your architecture and design choices
Judging
Judges:
1. Sachin Garg, Tech Lead @ Airbnb
2. Brihati Jain, Co- Founder @ Conqur AI
Format:
Area
Points
Answer accuracy
35
Citations and honesty
15
Production readiness
20
UX and easy embedding
15
Engineering (freshness, latency, cost)
15
All submissions are scored on the same test set after code freeze.
What we provide
A hack-day GitHub repo, with:
Setup steps to run OLake UI locally (
http://localhost:8000
, login
admin
/
password
)
Postgres seeded with small e-commerce tables (
orders
,
customers
,
payments
,
products
)
MinIO plus an Iceberg catalog as the destination
How to sign in and explore every API route in Swagger (
http://localhost:8000/swagger/index.html
)
The work, in three tiers
Core alone makes a complete entry; Stretch and Bonus are where strong entries stand out. Tool names and design are up to you.
Core:
read, run and diagnose existing pipelines
- List and inspect sources, destinations and jobs, with secrets masked
- Discover the tables in a source
- Trigger a sync and report progress until it finishes
- Diagnose a failed run from its logs (summarised, not dumped)
- Pause and resume a job
Stretch:
change pipelines
- Create a job: choose tables, sync mode (
full_refresh
,
incremental
,
cdc
) and schedule
- Configure each table on its own: sync mode, cursor field (for incremental), append or upsert, upsert type (equality deletes, position deletes, deletion vectors), partition regex, normalization and data filter. Offer only what that table supports, as returned by discovery
- Add a table or change a table's settings on an existing job. Warn and ask for confirmation when the change will clear that table's synced data
- Test and update a source's connection, and fix the broken job end to end
Bonus
- When a sync fails, suggest a concrete fix grounded in the OLake docs (for example, lower
max_threads
after an out-of-memory kill, or create the replication slot for Postgres CDC), and apply config fixes once the user confirms
- Destructive actions (delete a job, clear a destination) that refuse without the user's explicit confirmation
- OLake Fusion: list Iceberg tables with health details and enable maintenance
What to submit (by 6:30 PM)
MCP server
that starts with one command (
docker compose up
or
docker run
), listens on port 8080 with MCP over Streamable HTTP at
/mcp
, and reads
OLAKE_URL
,
OLAKE_USERNAME
and
OLAKE_PASSWORD
from the environment. We run every entry this way after code freeze, so this is required.
Your repo
, made public at submission with an MIT or Apache-2.0 license, and a README listing each tool, its inputs, its safety behaviour and which all tiers you completed.
Server-side safety is mandatory: mask secrets in every output and log line, and block destructive tools without an explicit confirmation.
Format
Individual
hackathon, in person. Choose Path A or Path B at check-in
Hacking runs from 10:45 AM to the 6:30 PM code freeze
Open to working professionals and university students
LLM API credits provided
Path B: bring a laptop with Docker installed (16 GB RAM recommended)
Top finalists from both paths present live to the judges.
Make your hackday smoother
Star OLake on
GitHub
for easy access to the repo
Skim the
OLake docs
so you know how we work
Check out the
OLake UI
repo to see how it works.
Join OLake on
Slack
to stay updated on events, PRs, contests, and more!
Happy hacking! #Hacktoberfest

description:
Join MoCo Code & Coffee for an afternoon hackathon as part of MLH's Hacktoberfest 2026! This year's theme is "AI Belongs to Everyone". Whether you've shipped models to production or have never touched one, you'll leave knowing more about open source AI and you'll have time to hack on your own project or collaborate with others.
Come solo, bring a team, or find one when you arrive. Beginners are very welcome. We'll have a short intro workshop, mentors on hand, and plenty of coffee and snacks to keep you going.
Space is limited, so please RSVP early.
Before You Arrive
Build time is short, so a little homework goes a long way:
Check out MLH resources for how to get started with open source models and APIs.
Join the Code & Coffee Discord to brainstorm ideas and find teammates ahead of time. Please follow the welcome instructions to add the DC/MD/VA role, and post questions to the #moco-general channel:
https://discord.gg/JbGyY3bKTS
Need inspiration? We'll share a list of beginner-friendly project ideas on the resource page (coming soon!).
What to Bring
A laptop and charger
Any accounts or API keys you plan to use, already set up
Your development environment ready to go (if you want to run a model locally, consider downloading it at home.)
An idea, or just curiosity
Location
We will be at Bethesda Green. This location is on the second floor of the Capital One Building. Enter the main building as if you are headed to Capital One, then go up the stairs to your right.
PLEASE NOTE: There is no working elevator at this time, stairs only.
4825 Cordell Avenue, Suite 200
Bethesda, Maryland 20814
More details about finding the space here:
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1bCMFlDXsPerKpshNFZa6b7AsOveYw-ol4cjT5brEadw/edit?usp=
The event will be held in the conference room and shared workspaces of Bethesda Green. Light refreshments and snacks will be provided.
Parking
Participants may park on the street or in nearby parking garages.
Public transit
Located near near the Bethesda metro station (Red Line).
Presenting Your Project
Sign up for a time slot at the event. The amount of time you'll have to present and time for Q&A will depend on the number of sign-ups we have. Your presentation should be to-the-point and cover three things:
What was your idea?
What did you accomplish?
What are your next steps?
Slides and a live demo are welcome but not required.
We encourage you to publish your code openly. That's what Hacktoberfest is about!
Prizes and Swag
MLH is providing prizes for the challenge categories, plus swag for participants. T-shirts and some other items are limited.
View the challenge categories on this page:
https://www.mlh.com/events/hacktoberfest-hack-day-bethesda-x-code-coffee-montgomery-county-md-chapter/challenges
Keep the Momentum Going
About an hour and a half isn't much build time, so treat this as a starting point! Bring your project to future Code & Coffee meetups to keep working on it with the community. For the rest of October, check out DEV Challenges, MLH livestreams, and Global Hack Week online.
Volunteer
Want to help out? We're looking for volunteers to staff check-in and mentor participants. Please consider signing up here:
https://www.signupgenius.com/go/9040D49AFA82DA5FB6-66417791-moco
Reach out with any questions on the Code & Coffee Discord in the #moco-general channel.

- Where keyword search and vector search each fall short

- How to add semantic search with vectors
- How to combine both into one hybrid search engine

🛠️ BrainerX Hack: Build What You Wish Existed
Fix a daily annoyance. Build a micro-tool. Ship it in 8 hours, proudly supported by MLH (Major League Hacking)
We’ve all been there: sitting at our desks, studying, coding, or managing our daily routine, and thinking, "Why isn't there a simple app, calculator, or tool that just fixes this one annoying thing?!"
Instead of waiting for someone else to build it, you are going to build it. The theme is simple: Build Something You Wish Existed. d. Think of those small, everyday inconveniences in student or student-developer life and create a clever micro-tool to solve them.
Whether it's a custom study timer with a personalised vibe, a quick GPA or grade calculator, a sleek link manager, a focus distraction blocker, or a custom flashcard app—this day is all about turning your daily pain points into a working solution.
No massive enterprise apps. No complex backend nightmares. Just smart, useful micro-tools built by you.
📅 Date: 20 October 2026
🕙 Time: 10:00 AM – 6:00 PM
📍 Venue:
BrainerX School, Constantine, Algeria
⏱️ Duration: 8 Hours

The day is designed as a complete, beginner-friendly hacking experience. You'll move smoothly from spotting an annoyance to prototyping to a live working tool, with plenty of support and peer learning along the way.
The event will include:
👥 Team Formation & Problem Storming: Share your daily frustrations and find people who want to solve them with you.
💡 Idea Scoping: Learn how to shrink a big idea into a tiny, achievable micro-tool you can actually finish in a few hours.
💻 Hands-On Coding Sessions: Write, style, and structure your app using frontend basics (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) or whatever tools you're learning.
🛠️ Mentorship & Guidance: Get help when you're stuck so you never feel left behind.
🎤 Show & Tell: Demonstrate your everyday fixer to the rest of the school.
🏆 Judging & Prizes: Recognition for the most clever, practical, and well-built micro-tools.

10:00 AM – 10:30 AM → Registration, Check-in & Welcome Coffee
10:30 AM – 11:00 AM → Opening, Theme Reveal & Problem-Solving Kickoff
11:00 AM – 1:30 PM → 🔥 Hacking Session 1: Laying down the UI and core logic
1:30 PM – 2:30 PM → 🍱 Lunch Break & Chill
2:30 PM – 4:30 PM → 🚀 Hacking Session 2: Polishing features and making it work

description:
Hacktoberfest Hacklab Turussa – tiistaina 20.10.
(english below)
Lokakuu on Hacktoberfest-kuukausi, ja me vietämme sitä avoimien ovien yhteydessä tiistaina 20.10. klo (viimeistään)18-20(aikaisintaan) osoitteessa Karjakatu 35b, Turku.
Hacktoberfest on maailmanlaajuinen kuukauden mittainen tapahtuma, jossa kannustetaan osallistumaan avoimen lähdekoodin projekteihin. Idea on yksinkertainen: etsit projektin, teet siihen parannuksen ja lähetät pull requestin. Ei tarvitse olla konkari — dokumentaation korjaus tai käännös on yhtä lailla kelvollinen kontribuutio kuin uusi ominaisuus.
Meillä paikan päällä:
apua ensimmäisen pull requestin tekoon, jos git ja GitHub eivät ole ennestään tuttuja
vinkkejä siitä, mistä löytää aloittelijaystävällisiä projekteja
hyvää seuraa, joka koodaa samassa tilassa
Ota oma läppäri mukaan. Tapahtuma on avoin kaikille, jäsenyyttä ei tarvita. Tervetuloa myös vain katsomaan, mitä labilla puuhataan.
October is Hacktoberfest month, and we're celebrating it as part of our open doors on Tuesday 20 October, from 18:00 (at the latest) to 20:00 (at the earliest), at Karjakatu 35b, Turku.
Hacktoberfest is a month-long global event that encourages people to contribute to open source projects. The idea is simple: find a project, make an improvement, and send a pull request. You don't need to be a veteran — fixing documentation or adding a translation counts just as much as a new feature.
On site we'll have:
help with your first pull request, if git and GitHub aren't familiar yet
tips on where to find beginner-friendly projects
good company coding in the same room
Bring your own laptop. The event is open to everyone, no membership required. You're also welcome to just drop by and see what we get up to at the lab.

You'll leave with a workflow you can adapt to your own open source edge AI project.

address:
95 cours Napoleon
CampusPlex
Ajaccio, Corsica 20000
France
description:
Hacktoberfest is back, and the 2026 edition focuses on open source AI. Instead of counting pull requests, this year is about building with open source tools and open-weight models — and about getting local communities together to do it.
GoodBarber is hosting the Ajaccio Fest: an after-work evening at CampusPlex, in the heart of the city. A talk on open source and open-weight AI — why it matters and concrete ways to get started, whether that means writing your first skills.md, running an open model locally, or building a small agent. Then questions, drinks and time to talk with the people around you.
No conference format, no pitch: just an excuse to get everyone in the same room on a weekday evening. Whether you already contribute to open source or have only been curious about where to start, come along.
The talk will be in French; slides and shared resources will be in English so you can keep going with the wider Hacktoberfest community afterwards.
Free to attend. Registration recommended.

title: Vibe Check: Agent Harnesses
description:
Melanie Warrick and Tom Wheeler host this episode of Vibe Check, with Jason Steving and Alex Tideman from Temporal demoing the new, experimental Temporal Agent Harness. They'll cover what a harness handles for you, why it matters once agents leave the demo stage, and when you don't need one at all.
You'll learn:
- What an agent harness is and what it takes care of
- Why durability matters once agents move past the demo
- How to tell when you don't need a harness
You'll leave knowing when a harness is worth reaching for in your own agents.

address:
20 Bendemeer Rd
#03-10 BS Bendemeer Centre
Singapore, Singapore 339914

description:
Hacktoberfest Singapore is a community meetup for anyone interested in open source, collaboration and building in the open.
The goal is simple: bring people together to share projects, exchange ideas, and find opportunities to contribute or collaborate. Whether you already maintain an open-source project, have a personal project you're thinking of open-sourcing, or want to make your first contribution, you're welcome to join.
The meetup will start with two featured talks, followed by an Open Space session where participants can propose topics, share projects, discuss ideas and form smaller groups around things they'd like to explore or work on together.
We hope the meetup helps more people:
Contribute to open-source projects
Find collaborators for personal or community projects
Open-source their own work
Meet others who are interested in building together
Embrace the idea of being open by default
Come with a project, an idea or simply an interest in open source.
Talks
A mix of talks and open spaces
Open Source for Everyone: Why (and How) to Take the Leap
By Jean-Phi
Open source is an integral part of our daily technological lives, whether it involves indispensable tools like GitLab and Mattermost, or languages and libraries like React and Quarkus. Taking the step to contribute remains an intimidating milestone for many people. However, pushing past this barrier and making that leap opens up very interesting opportunities, both on a human and technical part.
In this presentation, I will share my journey: from my very first contribution more than 8 years ago to the creation of my own open-source projects. My goal is to prove to you that anyone can contribute, whether you are a developer or not, and to give you the keys to get started with confidence.
Building with AI agents: 223 pull requests in 11 days
By Julien Dubois
A side project I never had time to build shipped in just 11 days — 223 merged pull requests, mostly written by AI agents working in parallel while I reviewed, guided, and merged. This talk breaks down how it was done, and whether it really counts.
Beyond the First PR: The Engineering Behind Maintaining Open Source
By Aishwarya Elango
What happens after you open-source a project?
Aishwarya will share her experience building and open-sourcing the WDS Operations Portal, and what it takes to make a codebase maintainable and contributor-friendly.
From a maintainer’s perspective, we’ll cover:
🏗️ System architecture — structure and key engineering decisions
🐛 Issues — creating clear bugs, enhancements, and first-time contributions
🔀 Pull requests — reviewing and deciding what is ready to merge
🧹 Code quality — evaluating correctness, security, readability, and maintainability
🧩 Codebase maintenance — managing technical debt, documentation, and project conventions
🌱 Contributor experience — making it easier for new developers to understand and contribute
A practical look at the engineering work behind maintaining an open-source project beyond the first PR.
Open space
Anyone can propose a topic, project, question or idea they'd like to discuss. We'll then break into smaller groups based on what people are interested in.
You could use the session to:
Share an open-source or personal project and find collaborators
Get feedback on something you're building
Discuss an open-source topic you care about
Find a project you'd like to contribute to
Meet others with similar interests and start building something together
You don't need to prepare anything in advance, and you don't need to be an open-source maintainer to participate. Bring a project, a question, an idea or just your curiosity.

description:
Ever wondered what's actually going on behind your favourite AI coding tools? The "harness" around a model is what turns it into something useful, and building one yourself is the best way to understand it. Join Talen to look under the hood and build one live from scratch.
You'll learn:
- What an AI harness does, and why open models need a little more support
- What existing open-source harnesses look like
- How to build a simple harness of your own around a local model
- Where to take it next to make it ready for real-world use
You'll leave understanding how AI tools work behind the scenes, with a starting point for building your own.

description:
Join Orlando Devs for a Hacktoberfest 2026 meetup!
From Hacktoberfest
"Hacktoberfest has always been about empowering people to build open software together. For years, that energy was measured by pull requests and developers making their first open-source contributions. But open source was never defined by a PR counter. Open source is a philosophy centered on transparency and collective ownership.
In an era where AI tools make low-effort PRs easier than ever to generate, maintainers face unprecedented volume and noise. This year, Hacktoberfest is focused on high-value, meaningful learning: giving everyone the tools and knowledge to experiment and build with open artificial intelligence.
By joining Hacktoberfest, online or in-person, you can expect to learn about open-weight models, open source agents, and more. We believe open innovation must be prioritized alongside proprietary tools for an ecosystem to remain healthy and resilient. Instead of counting PRs, you’ll write your first skills.md, build your own open-source agent, fine-tune an open-weight model, or go wherever your curiosity takes you.
Hacktoberfest 2026 is about meeting you wherever you are in your open source AI journey because we believe AI belongs to everyone."

Build an original project using open-source or open-weight AI, such as an agent skill, an app on an open-weight model, or an open-source model harness. Your project must be published in a public GitHub repository with an open-source license, and submitted through OrganizerHQ before the deadline.

Hacktoberfest-ийн олон улсын футболк, наалт, оролцогчийн багц
Өөрийгөө сорьж, шинэ хүмүүстэй танилцан инновацлаг шийдэл гаргах боломж

Oct 9–16: Registration
Oct 20–21: Online training — two webinars on how to build on top of erxes, focused on EdTech plugins
Oct 24: Build day — erxes Hub, Ulaanbaatar

Hacktoberfest 2026 global swag: t-shirt, stickers, participant pack
A chance to test yourself and build with like-minded people

Your plugin listed on erxes Marketplace, where builders sell to businesses

Bring a laptop.

title: Hacktoberfest Meetup Delhi X HackQube
address:
413/414 Forth floor, Tower B, PP TOWER, above Pind Baluchi, Netaji Subhash Place, Pitampura
New Delhi, Delhi 110034
India
description:
Hacktoberfest Meetup Delhi X HackQube is a free, one-day meetup about open source and open-source AI, organized by Humanoid Builder in collaboration with HackQube and hosted at Coding Blocks in Pitampura, Delhi.
📅 Monday, 24 October 2026 · 🕛 12:00 PM – 5:00 PM · 📍 Coding Blocks, PP Tower, Netaji Subhash Place, Pitampura · 🎟️ Free to attend
Hacktoberfest has run every October since 2014. In 2026 it moves away from counting pull requests and towards hands-on learning with open-source AI and open-weight models, through 300+ in-person events around the world. This meetup is one of them.
The day has four sessions:
🗣️ The real state of open source (about 35 minutes): how open source actually works in 2026, and how to contribute in ways maintainers value.
💻 Hands-on with Git and GitHub (about 60 minutes): branches, commits and pull requests, practised on your own laptop with mentors on the floor. This is the core workshop of the day.
🤖 Open-weight AI models (about 50 minutes): what open-weight means, and how to find, run and build with these models.
💼 Careers in the AI era (about 50 minutes): what teams hire for now, and how open-source work becomes your portfolio.
Speakers will be announced soon. Between and after sessions there is time to meet people, get help with your own repos, and make a first contribution with a mentor sitting next to you.
📈 Why now: India added over 5 million developers on GitHub in the past year and is now the largest open-source contributor base in the world (GitHub Octoverse 2025). A lot of that energy is in Delhi NCR, and this meetup is a low-pressure way to be part of it.
👥 Who it is for: college students in any year or branch, early-career developers, and anyone curious about open-source AI — designers, writers and founders included. No prior open-source experience is needed. Open to everyone aged 13+.
🎁 What you leave with: real Git practice, a clearer picture of open-weight AI, career advice from people who build and hire, and an official Hacktoberfest participation certificate. Free food and swag for attendees.
📍 Venue: Coding Blocks, PP Tower, Netaji Subhash Place, Pitampura — about a 5-minute walk from Netaji Subhash Place Metro (Red Line). Full address is in the location section below.
🎟️ 135+ people have already registered and seats are limited, so register early. Questions: use Contact Host on this page, or write to
[email protected]
.
Everyone at the event follows the MLH Code of Conduct:
https://mlh.io/code-of-conduct

title: Hacktoberfest Hack Day Roncade x H-FARM
address:
Via Adriano Olivetti, 1
La Serra
Roncade, Treviso 31056
Italy
description:
Hack for a day. Build it together. Leave it open for whoever comes next.
Hacktoberfest Hack Day Roncade x H-FARM
is a free, in-person Hack Day for people who want to build with open-source technologies, open-source AI, and open-weight models. Developers, designers, students, contributors, makers and tech enthusiasts: bring your laptop, your experience, or simply your curiosity, and spend a day turning an idea into something real.
This is not a day of slides, polished decks, or shipping four rushed pull requests. It’s about learning in public, collaborating across disciplines, and making a useful, creative, working project in only one day.
How the day works
You can arrive with a team or find one on the day. We will start with a few guiding challenges inspired by real needs, while leaving plenty of space for your own idea.
Hack time: design, prototype, code, test, rethink and keep going. Mentors with development, AI-model and design experience will be around throughout the day to help refine your perspective and exchange ideas. Short talks on creativity, open source/AI and design will give you fresh input at key moments.
At the end, every team will publish its project with an open-source license and a README, then show the product in a relaxed demo and networking session. No pitch deck required: let what you built do the talking.
What we value
We are not looking for the biggest or most complicated project. We care about:
a useful or genuinely creative idea;
thoughtful use of open-source technology, open-source AI or open-weight models;
a working, well-crafted product and a clear demo;
design and UX (not only code);
openness: an open-source license and a README that makes it easy for others to continue the work;
the journey: the choices, pivots, discoveries and collaboration behind the project.
Who is it for?
Everyone who is excited to build: tech enthusiasts, software engineers, architects, designers, open-source contributors and maintainers, students, startup and company professionals and people who are simply ready to experiment. You do not need to be an AI expert or a seasoned open-source contributor. Mixed teams are encouraged, and non-technical perspectives matter.
What to bring
Bring your laptop, a charger, and an open mind, we’ll take care of the rest: space, Wi-Fi, power, mentors, and the fuel to keep you going. Come ready to build; we’ll make sure no one hacks on an empty stomach. ;)
Registration
Participation is free. Registration and the final event details will be shared through the official Hacktoberfest Fest page.
Legal notice
By attending the event, you authorize the organizers to take photographs and video recordings and to use this material for documentation, communication, and promotional purposes related to Hacktoberfest and H-FARM.
See you at H-FARM. Let’s turn bold ideas into open-source projects others can build on.

address:
