description:
Hacktoberfest Hack Day Barcelona
On October 24, we're getting together at Plata's Barcelona office for a one-day, in-person hackathon as part of Hacktoberfest 2026, a global technology festival organized by Major League Hacking (MLH) and DEV.
This year's theme is open-source AI and open-weight models. You'll have 5 hours to turn an idea into a working prototype. Using AI tools while you build isn't just allowed, it's encouraged.
CHALLENGES
Your project needs to fit at least one challenge, and you can compete in several at once. Full details are in the Prize Categories section.
Best Open-Source AI Project — the festival's main challenge
Build a project where open-source or open-weight AI is an important part of how it works. It could be an agent skill, a product built on an open-weight LLM or SLM, or your own or an improved open-source model harness. The project must be published in a public GitHub repository under an open-source license.
Best Use of Gemma 4 — by Google DeepMind
Gemma 4 is a lightweight, multimodal open-weight model you can access through the Gemini API. Use it to build an assistant that understands both text and images, a focused AI tool for learning, creativity, or productivity, or simply to move fast from idea to prototype. Getting-started resources are in the Links & Resources section.
A Judge That Learns from an Expert — Plata Bank Challenge
Evaluating AI products is increasingly handed off to LLM-as-a-judge models. The problem: their idea of a good answer often doesn't match that of a domain expert who knows the product, the rules of the field, and what users actually need. Today, the judge prompt is usually tuned by hand, a couple of cases at a time. Your challenge is to automate that process. You'll get an expert-labeled dataset and the same metric script used for final scoring; solutions are judged on hidden-test quality, cost, and speed.
Best Use of ElevenLabs
Give your AI a voice. Build a voice agent, a creative audio experience, or a practical tool powered by speech recognition or text-to-speech. ElevenLabs should be a meaningful part of the project, not decoration.
PRIZES
For all participants:
— 1 free month of ElevenLabs Creator (131k credits)
— 25% off a General Attendee ticket to Web Summit 2026 (valid for one week after the hackathon)
For every member of the winning teams in all challenges:
— a YubiKey 5 NFC or 5C NFC from Yubico
— access to the online stream of Matemarketing and recordings from previous years
Plus, by challenge:
1. Best Open-Source AI Project — 3 passes to Web Summit 2026 in Lisbon (Nov 9–12), 3 months of ElevenLabs Pro for each team member (600k credits/month), DEV Badges, and an MLH swag bag
2. Best Use of Gemma 4 — [prize TBA]
3. A Judge That Learns from an Expert:
— The winning team receives an exclusive consultation with Plata’s Head of AI Engineering, available online or in person, online career consultation with a Plata Talent Acquisition Specialist.
— The prize-winning team receives an online consultation with Plata’s Head of AI Engineering
4. Best Use of ElevenLabs — 3 months of ElevenLabs Scale for each team member (1.8M credits/month)
PARTNERS
MLH & DEV, Plata, Google DeepMind, DigitalOcean, ElevenLabs, Web Summit, Yubico, Matemarketing.
HOW IT WORKS
Team up — up to 3 people. Come with your own team, find teammates in advance in our Telegram chat, or team up on the day. Solo is fine too.
Pick an idea — no need to bring a ready-made project: per the official Hacktoberfest rules, work on your submission has to start at the event.
Build — 5 hours to design, build, and polish a working prototype.
Demo & judging — show what you built, get feedback from the judges, and the best projects take home prizes.
WHO IS THIS FOR?
AI and ML engineers, developers, and anyone who can and wants to build products on AI models. If your notes are full of ideas you never get around to, these are your 5 hours.
📍 Plata office, Edifici Colom, Av. de les Drassanes, 6, Floor 15, Barcelona
📅 Saturday, October 24, 2026
⏱ 11:00–18:00, check-in from 10:30
💬 Telegram chat: t.me/hacktoberfest_bcn

description:
Hacktoberfest Hack Day Rabat
Break through. Build open.
One free day. Your team. A real project built with open-source AI.
Hacktoberfest is the worldwide celebration of open source, and in 2026 it is about building with open-source AI: open-source tools and open-weight models. It is organized by Major League Hacking (MLH) and DEV, in partnership with DigitalOcean. On Saturday 24 October, ForgeBots Club hosts the Rabat edition: a one-day, in-person hack day at the College of Computing, UM6P. Despite the word "hack", this is a building day, not a cybersecurity event. You form a team, build something new, and present it.
What you'll do
Create a new project during the day, publish it in a public GitHub repository with an open-source licence, and demo it to the judges.
Two challenges
(a project may enter both)
-
Best Open-Source AI Project:
an original project where open-source or open-weight AI is an important part of how it works.
-
Best Use of Gemma 4:
a project that genuinely uses a Gemma 4 model (an open-weight model) through the Gemini API.
What you get
- You leave with a great project: a working build, a public GitHub repository with your name on it, and a demo you can show anyone.
- An official Hacktoberfest participation certificate for every checked-in participant.
- Two prizes, one for the winner of each challenge. The winners of Best Open-Source AI Project also earn a DEV Badge.
Who can join
Open to UM6P students only, from any field and any experience level. No prior hackathon or AI experience is needed. Teams of one to four: come with your team, or arrive alone and form one on the day.
Registration, check-in and submission
- Registration and check-in are individual: every team member must register and check in on the day.
- Submission is per team: only one teammate submits the project, on behalf of the whole team.
Before the day
Create a MyMLH account, a GitHub account, and a DEV account linked to MyMLH. For Gemma entries, get a free Gemini API key. Bring your laptop and charger.
Schedule
- 09:00 — Check-in and team formation
- 09:30 — Welcome, Code of Conduct, challenges, and rules
- 09:50 — Short open-source AI demonstration
- 10:10 — Project work begins; mentors circulate
- 20:30 — Submission support desk
- 21:00 — Submission deadline (OrganizerHQ closes)
- After 21:00 — Team demos and judging begin, right after the submission deadline
- 22:40 — Results, awards, and closing
- 23:15 — End
Good to know
Free to attend. Eligibility is checked first: a polished demo cannot make up for missing a challenge requirement. Questions:

description:
Zero Day in Nsukka: Building with Open-Source AI
Open-source innovation has entered a defining era. For Hacktoberfest 2026, the focus has evolved from counting pull requests to high-impact experimentation, decentralized intelligence, and practical builder education.
Hosted by Dewdrop Labs, we want to bring together developers, engineers, and tech enthusiasts across the region for an intensive, hands-on session exploring modern open-weight artificial intelligence models, autonomous agent frameworks, and collaborative open-source toolchains. Whether you are running local models, fine-tuning lightweight architectures, or diving into open-source for the very first time, this hack day is designed to bridge foundational understanding with production-grade engineering.
What to Expect
Open-Weight Architectures & Tooling: Understand the technical trade-offs between closed APIs and open-weight models, and explore how to deploy and infer locally without proprietary lock-in.
Agentic Workflows & Collaboration: Hands-on walkthroughs covering skills specification, open-source AI tooling, and building autonomous agent pipelines.
Interactive Code & Lightning Demos: Bring your laptop to hack on live projects, test configurations, share insights, and get peer feedback in real time.
Networking & Swag: Connect with fellow regional developers, contribute to the ecosystem, and celebrate Hacktoberfest with the local dev community.

Join us for Myrtle Beach’s first in-person Hacktoberfest Hack Day, hosted in partnership with eMYRge!

🤝 Meet and collaborate with other local tech enthusiasts

🤖 Explore AI and what it means to make the technology accessible to everyone
💻 Build, experiment, and contribute to open source
🧠 Learn from others and share what you know
🌴 Spend the day hacking with the Myrtle Beach tech community
Whether you’re here to build something ambitious, make your first open-source contribution, or just see what Hacktoberfest is all about, there’s a place for you at Hack Day.
Come with an idea. Come with a skill. Come with questions. Or just come curious.
AI belongs to everyone. So does Hacktoberfest.
Happy Hacking!

description:
The AI Collective Portland presents Hack for Humanity, part of a global civic hackathon running across 120+ chapters in 50+ countries this fall.
​Spend a Saturday building with Google Gemini to take on meaningful human and community challenges. This event continues the Humans in AI Week conversations from this summer, where communities named the problems that matter most to them. Every project should create impact close to home, with the purpose of benefiting humanity.
​Local action, global impact
We're gathering here in Portland, but we're building alongside partners and communities around the world. What you make on Saturday can serve your neighbors and reach a town thousands of miles away. That connection is the heart of this event.
​Pick your lane
Every team chooses one of three builds. Space in each lane is capped, so everyone lands somewhere.
​1. Census tool (Pijao, Colombia): An offline-first, bilingual tool that helps volunteers record household impact after the earthquake and decide who gets aid first.
​2. Transparency dashboard (Portland local track): A public dashboard that shows how funds and project phases are moving for a Portland nonprofit. The same tool will carry over to relief work in Colombia.
​Who should come: Engineers, designers, PMs, researchers and curious beginners. No team or idea needed. We'll help you find both.
​Recognition: Winning projects may be featured in The AI Collective newsletter, reaching 300,000+ subscribers.

description:
Our event is a technical roundtable on open source solutions for running AI workers reliably in production. AI workers (autonomous agents that call tools, run long tasks, and act on real systems) are moving from demos into production, and the infrastructure to run them dependably is still being worked out in the open. The roundtable brings practitioners together to map that stack and the OSS projects filling each layer.
We will run it in three parts:
Framing (about 15 minutes): a short setup of what a reliable AI worker stack needs, covering orchestration, observability and tracing, guardrails and policy enforcement, durability and retries, and evaluation.
Roundtable (60 to 75 minutes): a facilitated discussion where practitioners compare the open source tools they use at each layer, where the gaps are, and what is worth building. It is led by people who work on agent reliability infrastructure day to day.
Hacktoberfest contribution (45 minutes): attendees pick relevant OSS projects, triage good first issues together, and open pull requests on the spot, with experienced contributors helping newcomers land their first merged PR.
Everyone leaves with a clearer map of the open source AI infrastructure landscape and at least one contribution in progress.

description:
Hack Night: Rust meets AI
AI is everywhere right now, and Rust has quietly become one of its most interesting companions. Rust's speed, memory safety and small footprint make it a natural fit for running models efficiently, on everything from servers to ordinary laptops. A growing ecosystem of Rust crates now makes it possible to load and run open-weight models directly, without Python, cloud services or API keys.
This Hack Night is about exploring that intersection. Maybe you're curious how AI models actually run under the hood. Maybe you want to see what Rust brings to machine learning, or you just want to build something fun with AI running locally on your own machine. Whatever the reason, this evening is for you.
No prior AI experience is needed, and you don't need a powerful computer. Everything we'll work with runs on a normal laptop without a GPU. Beginners and experienced Rustaceans are equally welcome, and we'll help each other along the way.
The event is part of Hacktoberfest 2026, a global celebration of open source.
As always, we end the evening with a short show-and-tell, where anyone who wants to can share what they built.
Bring your laptop and your curiosity!
Food
Please notice that this event does not include any food, so make sure to refuel before you arrive. Please also notice that we are not allowed to bring our own food.
Location
The room is named "Opholdsstue 1" in Folkehuset Møllestien, Grønnegade 10, Aarhus.
Continue straight through the main entrance, and then it is on your left.
If you arrive late, the main entrance will be locked. In that case, follow the facade 2/3 down Grønnegade and knock on the window, and we will let you in through the main entrance.

description:
Hacktoberfest 2026 — Student Open Source Hack Day
Let's gather for a student-focused open-source hacking experience where students can learn, build, collaborate, and make meaningful contributions to real-world projects.
Whether you're making your first open-source contribution or already familiar with GitHub, this event is an opportunity to learn by doing, connect with fellow student developers, and experience the open-source community.
Students can participate individually or form small teams based on their interests and skills, work on open-source projects, and receive guidance throughout the event.
Event Structure & Agenda
Kickoff & Hacktoberfest Briefing
Welcome students, introduce Hacktoberfest and the fundamentals of open-source contribution, and explain how students can participate. Share project repositories, contribution guidelines, GitHub resources, and useful learning materials.
Idea Sharing & Team Formation
Students share project or contribution ideas, discuss areas they're interested in, ask questions, and form teams based on complementary skills and interests. Students who prefer to work independently can also choose their own open-source project.
Hacking & Mentorship Session
Students spend dedicated time exploring repositories, understanding codebases, fixing bugs, improving documentation, adding features, and creating pull/merge requests. Mentors and experienced student contributors provide guidance on Git, GitHub, code reviews, debugging, and contribution best practices.
Student Demos & Showcase
Students showcase what they built or contributed during the event. Each participant or team can give a short demo highlighting their contribution, the problem they worked on, what they learned, and the pull/merge request they submitted.
Wrap-Up & Student Networking
Celebrate student contributions and participation, share key learnings, and recognize notable projects and contributions. Students can connect with other developers, exchange ideas, discover new open-source projects, and find opportunities to continue contributing together.
Come learn, build, contribute, and grow with open source!
Happy hacking! 🚀

description:
OSAI Workshop — From First PR to AI Contributor
Join a hands-on Hacktoberfest Meetup focused on exploring and contributing to AI and Machine Learning open-source projects.
This event is designed as a continuation of our open-source initiative, taking participants beyond the basics of GitHub and into the real-world workflows of AI open-source communities. Whether you're making your first contribution or already familiar with Git and GitHub, you'll have the opportunity to explore real projects, meet project leads and mentors, and find a contribution that matches your interests and skill level.
What to Expect
AI Open Source 101 — Understand how AI/ML open-source communities and projects work.
Project Showcase — Explore AI projects developed within the IEEE RGIPT Student Branch GitHub community.
Repository Deep Dive — Learn how to navigate an unfamiliar AI codebase, understand its architecture, and identify contribution opportunities.
Good First Issues — Discover beginner-friendly issues and learn how to approach them.
Project Mentorship — Meet Project Leads and Mentors who will guide you through project setup, codebases, and your first contributions.
GitHub Workflow — Work with issues, branches, commits, pull requests, reviews, and collaborative development.
Hacktoberfest Contributions — Take your first step toward contributing to a real open-source project.
Community & Networking — Connect with students working on AI, ML, and open-source projects.
What Happens After Hacktoberfest?
The Meetup is designed to be more than a one-day contribution sprint. Participants can continue working with their selected projects, progressing from Good First Issues → First PRs → Bug Fixes → Feature Contributions → Long-Term Project Participation.
This initiative will also serve as an introduction to Winter of Code, a separate and larger open-source initiative where participants can take their contributions further.
Learn the project. Meet the community. Make your first contribution. Build beyond the PR.
No prior open-source contribution experience is required. Bring your curiosity, your laptop, and your interest in AI—we'll help you find a place to start.

description:
Uma tarde para transformar um problema concreto em um protótipo funcional com IA de código aberto ou modelos de pesos abertos. Pessoas com diferentes níveis de experiência são bem-vindas: você pode chegar com uma equipe ou formar uma no evento.
As equipes poderão escolher um dos desafios preparados pela organização:
Finanças pessoais: analisar despesas de exemplo e destacar um padrão que mereça atenção.
Tarefas do dia a dia: transformar anotações desorganizadas em tarefas e ajudar a decidir o próximo passo.
Informações de projetos: encontrar respostas em notas e questões de diferentes projetos, indicando as fontes usadas.
Também será possível propor outro problema, desde que a equipe consiga definir para quem está construindo, quais dados usará e o que demonstrará até o fim do dia.
O trabalho no projeto começa durante o evento. Cada equipe deverá apresentar um protótipo, publicar o código em um repositório público no GitHub com licença de código aberto e instruções de uso, e enviar o projeto pela área Challenges do OrganizerHQ antes das demonstrações. Os projetos concorrerão ao desafio Best Open-Source AI Project.
Traga um laptop e carregador, se tiver. A Unimontes disponibilizará computadores para participantes que precisarem.

description:
Attention : cet événement est une expérience immersive de 12h (12h-00h). Ne vous inscrivez que si vous pouvez garantir votre présence du début à la fin pour préserver l'énergie du groupe et ne pas bloquer une place limitée ! (Un créneau dédié au networking court sera proposé séparément).
Pour la première fois, Hacktoberfest arrive dans les Alpes françaises !
Pendant 12 heures, nous allons réunir à Annecy développeurs, AI builders, contributeurs open source, entrepreneurs et entreprises locales autour d'un même objectif : se rencontrer, apprendre les uns des autres et construire des projets concrets grâce à l'IA et à l'open source.
Et pas besoin d'arriver avec une équipe déjà constituée. Le principe du hackathon est justement de faire se rencontrer ceux qui ont des problèmes à résoudre, ceux qui ont des idées, ceux qui savent construire et ceux qui ont simplement envie d'apprendre en construisant.
Vous pouvez venir avec un case d'usage mais sans développeur : une tâche répétitive, un processus interne, un workflow client ou un problème métier que vous aimeriez automatiser. Vous rencontrerez sur place des AI builders et développeurs qui cherchent justement des problèmes réels sur lesquels travailler, expérimenter et apprendre.
À l'inverse, vous pouvez venir en tant que porteur de projets sans projet précis en tête. Pas besoin d'avoir la prochaine grande idée de startup. Venez avec vos compétences, votre curiosité et l'envie de construire : nous vous aiderons à rencontrer des entrepreneurs et des entreprises qui ont des problèmes concrets à résoudre.
Et si vous êtes déjà développeur, AI builder ou profil tech au sein d'une entreprise, vous pouvez évidemment venir avec votre propre équipe et votre propre use case.
Le hackathon sera organisé autour de deux grands tracks.
--- TECH FOR BUSINESS : Mettre l'IA au service de l'économie locale ---
Vous avez un problème métier et cherchez des personnes capables de vous aider à le prototyper ? Venez avec votre use case, nous vous aiderons à former une équipe autour de vous. PME, artisans, commerces, indépendants et entreprises industrielles pourront apporter une tâche répétitive, un processus interne, un workflow client ou tout autre problème opérationnel qu'ils aimeraient automatiser.
Mais Tech for Business s'adresse aussi aux entreprises qui ont déjà les compétences pour construire en interne.
Vous êtes développeur, AI builder, CTO, product manager ou membre d'une équipe tech et vous avez depuis des mois ce projet IA que vous n'avez jamais le temps de prototyper ? Prenez ces 12 heures pour construire pour votre propre entreprise. Venez seul ou avec vos collègues, choisissez une problématique métier réelle et profitez du hackathon comme d'un espace entièrement dédié pour passer de l'idée au prototype.
Dans les deux cas, l'objectif est le même : partir d'un vrai problème métier et essayer, en 12 heures, d'arriver à un premier agent, un prototype ou un plan de déploiement concret.
Et surtout, vous construirez au milieu d'autres équipes confrontées aux mêmes questions, avec des spécialistes présents pour vous accompagner, challenger vos choix et vous aider lorsque vous bloquez. Même si vous venez pour construire pour votre propre entreprise, vous venez aussi pour apprendre des autres.
--- TECH FOR OPEN SOURCE : Mettre l'IA au service de l'open source ---
Le deuxième track sera consacré à celles et ceux qui souhaitent utiliser l'agentic coding pour augmenter leur capacité à contribuer à des projets open source.
Choisissez un projet, formez une équipe et utilisez les outils d'IA pour comprendre une codebase, résoudre des issues, écrire des tests, améliorer la documentation, développer de nouvelles fonctionnalités ou simplement faire avancer un projet auquel vous avez envie de contribuer.
Et dans les deux tracks, vous ne serez pas seuls face à votre ordinateur.
Parce que parfois, 12 heures à construire avec les bonnes personnes valent mieux qu'une conférence, une formation ou une journée de slides.
Ce n'est donc pas seulement un hackathon. C'est aussi un moment de rencontre entre des personnes qui, autrement, ne se seraient peut-être jamais retrouvées autour de la même table : entreprises locales, entrepreneurs, développeurs, spécialistes de l'IA et contributeurs open source.
Venez avec un problème, une idée, un projet, vos compétences ou simplement l'envie de construire. On formera les équipes sur place.
Et 12 heures plus tard, l'objectif est simple : avoir appris quelque chose, rencontré de nouvelles personnes et surtout… développer quelque chose de concret.

description:
Hacktoberfest - Lucknow AI Labs,
Saturday, 31 October 2026 · Lucknow · In person
Hosted by AI Community Lucknow and Lucknow AI Labs, in collaboration with Major League Hacking
The last day of Hacktoberfest. One room, one day, and whatever it takes to get your pull requests merged before the month runs out.
Hacktoberfest is a month-long celebration of open source, and most people start it with good intentions and finish it at 11 PM on the 31st. This is that night, except you're not doing it alone. Bring your laptop, find an issue, and ship it with maintainers and experienced contributors sitting next to you.
Who this is for
Complete beginners who have never opened a pull request and want their first one merged, and experienced contributors closing out their final PRs. Both work here. If you have never touched open source before, the first session is built for you.
What happens on the day
Onboarding for first-timers: Git and GitHub basics, how to fork, branch, commit and open a pull request, and how to read a contributing guide
Issue matching: we help you find issues that fit your skill level and language, from documentation to real bug fixes
Contribute to UPAI Labs projects: our own open-source repositories, including NAWAB AI, LucknowLLM, UPAI RAG, Sign Language Translator and lucknow-live-events, with maintainers in the room to review your PR on the spot
Contribute anywhere: work on any Hacktoberfest-participating project you like
Maintainer support: experienced contributors help you unblock, review your work and improve your PR before you submit
Live leaderboard: track merged PRs through the day
What you need to bring
A laptop with Git installed and a GitHub account
A Hacktoberfest registration. Register at hacktoberfest.com and check this year's rules and PR requirements before you arrive.
Any language or stack. Documentation contributions count too.
What you leave with
Merged pull requests, your name in project histories, the confidence to contribute again in November, and a network of people who do this regularly. Contributors to UPAI Labs projects who keep going are invited into our maintainer group.
Free to attend. Limited seats.

description:
Hacktoberfest 2026 — Student Open Source Hack Day
Let's gather for a student-focused open-source hacking experience where students can learn, build, collaborate, and make meaningful contributions to real-world projects.
Whether you're making your first open-source contribution or already familiar with GitHub, this event is an opportunity to learn by doing, connect with fellow student developers, and experience the open-source community.
Students can participate individually or form small teams based on their interests and skills, work on open-source projects, and receive guidance throughout the event.
Event Structure & Agenda
Kickoff & Hacktoberfest Briefing
Welcome students, introduce Hacktoberfest and the fundamentals of open-source contribution, and explain how students can participate. Share project repositories, contribution guidelines, GitHub resources, and useful learning materials.
Idea Sharing & Team Formation
Students share project or contribution ideas, discuss areas they're interested in, ask questions, and form teams based on complementary skills and interests. Students who prefer to work independently can also choose their own open-source project.
Hacking & Mentorship Session
Students spend dedicated time exploring repositories, understanding codebases, fixing bugs, improving documentation, adding features, and creating pull/merge requests. Mentors and experienced student contributors provide guidance on Git, GitHub, code reviews, debugging, and contribution best practices.
Student Demos & Showcase
Students showcase what they built or contributed during the event. Each participant or team can give a short demo highlighting their contribution, the problem they worked on, what they learned, and the pull/merge request they submitted.
Wrap-Up & Student Networking
Celebrate student contributions and participation, share key learnings, and recognize notable projects and contributions. Students can connect with other developers, exchange ideas, discover new open-source projects, and find opportunities to continue contributing together.
Come learn, build, contribute, and grow with open source!
Happy hacking! 🚀

The Arduino UNO Q unlocks a new level of performance for the Arduino ecosystem, blending robust computing power from Qualcomm's advanced Dragonwing™ QRB2210 MPU running a full Debian Linux OS with upstream support, and the real-time responsiveness of a dedicated STM32U585 MCU running Arduino sketches over Zephyr OS - all on a single-board computer.

The Arduino® UNO Q integrates the Qualcomm® QRB2210 Microprocessor (MPU), running a full Debian-based Linux environment, with the STMicroelectronics® STM32U585 Microcontroller (MCU) built on Arm® Cortex®-M33 architecture, all within the compact UNO form factor. This dual-architecture platform combines high-performance computing with deterministic real-time control, delivering the power and versatility needed for modern AI at the edge applications.

Unlock hybrid development with Arduino App Lab, seamlessly uniting Python applications, Arduino sketches, and AI models in a single workflow. From AI-powered vision and sound solutions that react intelligently to their environment to sophisticated smart home systems, UNO Q with Arduino App Lab delivers next-generation embedded innovation to makers, educators, and professionals alike. At the same time, developers enjoy true freedom of choice: program the MCU subsystem with the Arduino IDE, or integrate Arduino CLI into existing workflows with popular editors like VS Code.

Documentation and technical-writing contributors

Anyone looking to start contributing to open source

Our Objective
The goal of Hacktoberfest Hack Day is to make open source
accessible, collaborative, and approachable for everyone
.
By the end of the event, participants should have practical experience with collaborative development workflows, a better understanding of Git and GitHub, and—most importantly—the confidence to continue contributing to open-source projects beyond the event.

A laptop with Git installed

Your curiosity and willingness to learn
Your ideas and enthusiasm for open source
Come together with fellow developers, make meaningful contributions, learn from the community, and celebrate the spirit of open source.

description:
Welcome to PolyTech Code Fest 2026! ❤️
Join us on October 31 in Lviv for PolyTech Code Fest — a free, in-person student hackathon held as part of Hacktoberfest 2026 under the aegis of Major League Hacking (MLH). For the first time in Ukraine! 🇺🇦
The event is organized by the Collegium and the Student and Postgraduate Union of Lviv Polytechnic National University, in partnership with SKELAR — an investment company and platform for tech businesses that helps teams build and scale products for global markets.
The Challenge: Build an MVP in One Day ⚡
No prepared ideas or projects needed. The hackathon challenge will be revealed at the start of the event.
Your mission? Team up, turn an idea into a working prototype, and pitch your solution to the jury by the end of the day.
You can use open-source libraries, frameworks, AI models, and APIs to bring your solution to life.
Who Can Join? 🎯
We welcome students majoring in technical fields at any university in Ukraine who are currently in:
• Years 2–4 of their Bachelor's degree;
• Year 1 of their Master's degree.
You don't need previous hackathon experience, but you should have your own projects to showcase on GitHub or GitLab.
Participation is free.
Team Format 👥
Apply as a team of 2–4 or go solo — we'll help you find teammates!
What to Expect 💡
• Team Challenge: Build an MVP based on a challenge announced at the start of the hackathon.
• Mentorship: Get guidance and feedback from mentors as you develop your solution.
• Tech Talk by SKELAR: Gain insights from a company building and scaling tech businesses for global markets.
• Final Pitch: Present your working prototype to the jury and demonstrate what your team has built.
• Prizes & Opportunities: Compete for prizes from the organizers. Outstanding participants will also have the opportunity to receive additional scholarship* from SKELAR — 10 000 UAH per month for 10 calculated months.
Scholarship recipients will be selected separately after the event. The selection will not be based on hackathon rankings or competition results.
*The term “scholarship” refers to the provision of monthly financial assistance as part of the Participant Support Program for one academic year (10 calendar months).
How Does Selection Work? 🔍
You don't need to prepare a hackathon project in advance.
To apply, complete the registration form and include a link to your GitHub or GitLab profile featuring your own work. This is a mandatory part of the application.
Our team will review applications and repositories to select participants. Spots are limited, so submitting the form does not automatically guarantee a place at the event.
Selected participants will receive confirmation and the exact venue address.
Event Details 📍
• Date: October 31, 2026
• Time: 09:00–21:00
• Location: Lviv, Ukraine (in person). The exact address will be shared with selected participants.
• Participation: Free
• Registration deadline: October 26, 2026, at 14:00 (Kyiv time).
What to Bring 🎒
• Your laptop and charger.
• Access to your GitHub or GitLab account.
• Your curiosity and readiness to build something with a team.
Code of Conduct 📜
We are committed to creating a welcoming, respectful, and collaborative environment for every participant. All attendees must follow the applicable Hacktoberfest and MLH Codes of Conduct.
Ready to turn your tech skills into a working product? Apply now and join us at PolyTech Code Fest! 🔥

description:
Join Cod3rs and IT Women Esbjerg for a Hacktoberfest Hack Day - a one-day, in person event, celebrating open-source culture and modern tech.
What is it about?
Our goal is to create an inclusive space to work on open-source projects, learn about open AI tools, share knowledge, and collaborate on real code. Whether you are a seasoned professional, a curious student, or a complete beginner without a clue where to start, this is your chance to build and ship something real using open-source or open-weight AI.
What to bring?
All you need to bring is a laptop, a charger, and some enthusiasm. Have an exciting idea? Awesome! Still missing one? No worries, we'll have challenges ready at the door so you can borrow an idea.
How does it work?
Once you have decided which idea to pursue, you get to spend the day turning the idea into a working project. Fuel it with pizza, coffee, and snacks. Submit through OrganizerHQ Challenges and go head-to-head in the Best Open-Source AI Project challenge. First pull request or fiftieth, you're in the right room!
Sounds scary? 👻
Don't worry, even though the event lands on Halloween, there is nothing to be afraid of. You can join ranks with other people, and form teams to help each other (don't let merge conflicts haunt you though). Plus, our friendly volunteers will be on hand all day to help whenever you get stuck.
Share your pics and screenshots with #Hacktoberfest. Happy hacking!

venue_name: Centro de Competência em Software Livre (CCSL), IME-USP
address:

description:
[pt-BR]
E se, neste Halloween, em vez de caçar fantasmas, você caçasse bugs? No dia 31 de outubro, o FLUSP — FLOSS at USP recebe a Hacktoberfest 2026 para um dia de experimentação, aprendizado e construção coletiva no CCSL, no IME-USP.
A edição deste ano da Hacktoberfest tem um novo foco: Open-Source AI. Em vez de simplesmente contar pull requests, a proposta é colocar a mão no código, explorar modelos open-weight, ferramentas de IA open source e agentes, aprender junto e construir coisas de verdade.
E não poderia haver lugar melhor para isso. O FLUSP é uma comunidade de estudantes da USP dedicada a contribuir com projetos de software livre, com uma cultura baseada em compartilhamento de conhecimento, revisão de código, mentoria e colaboração. O grupo mantém encontros semanais no CCSL, um espaço do IME dedicado justamente à promoção do software livre.
Durante o Hack Day, vamos transformar essa filosofia em prática: formar equipes, experimentar ideias, construir projetos e aprender com outras pessoas. Você não precisa ser especialista em IA nem chegar com um projeto pronto — basta trazer curiosidade, vontade de construir e, de preferência, seu laptop.
E sim: é Halloween. Então venha preparado para encontrar alguns bugs assustadores, modelos que fazem coisas inexplicáveis e, quem sabe, um ou outro merge sobrenatural.
Código aberto, ideias abertas e um sábado inteiro para construir. Nos vemos no Hack Day!
[en]
What better way to spend Halloween than hunting bugs instead of ghosts? On October 31st, FLUSP — FLOSS at USP is hosting Hacktoberfest 2026 for a full day of experimentation, learning, and collaborative building at the CCSL, at IME-USP.
This year's Hacktoberfest comes with a new focus: Open-Source AI. Instead of simply counting pull requests, the goal is to get hands-on with open-weight models, open-source AI tools, and agents — learning together, experimenting, and actually building things.
There couldn't be a better place for it. FLUSP is a community of USP students dedicated to contributing to free and open-source software, with a culture built around knowledge sharing, code review, mentoring, and collaboration. The group holds weekly meetings at the CCSL, a space at IME dedicated to fostering free and open-source software.
During the Hack Day, we'll put that philosophy into practice: form teams, explore ideas, build projects, and learn from one another. You don't need to be an AI expert or arrive with a fully formed project — bring your curiosity, your willingness to build, and, preferably, your laptop.
And yes: it's Halloween. So be ready for terrifying bugs, mysterious model behavior, and maybe even a supernatural merge.
Open code, open ideas, and a whole Saturday to build. See you at Hack Day!

Python Panamá presenta Hacktoberfest Hack Day Panama City. Primeros Pasos – Para quienes nunca han tocado código, o ni siquiera saben qué es GitHub. address:

Portland, Oregon 97201
United States
description:
Join us for a Hacktoberfest community event focused on learning, collaboration, and open-source contribution. Whether you’re new to open source or an experienced contributor, this is an opportunity to connect with fellow developers, explore real-world projects, and build together.
Throughout the event, participants will have the opportunity to:
Learn how to get started with open source and make meaningful contributions
Discover and contribute to projects that align with their interests
Collaborate with fellow developers and community members
Work on pull requests, issues, and other open-source contributions
Share knowledge, ideas, and experiences with the community
Meet new people and grow their developer network
The event is designed to be welcoming to developers of all experience levels. You don’t need to be an open-source expert to participate—just bring your curiosity, willingness to learn, and a desire to build something together.
Whether you join us in person, online, or through a combination of both, come ready to learn, collaborate, contribute, and connect.
Let’s celebrate open source and make Hacktoberfest a month of meaningful contributions and community-driven learning!
Learn more about Hacktoberfest events at
https://hacktoberfest.com/events
.

address:
KANPUR, UTTAR PRADESH 209217
India
description:
🎃 Hacktoberfest 2026: Spooky Open-Source AI Hack Day
Get ready for a spooktacular day of coding, innovation, and open-source contribution! Join us for an official Major League Hacking (MLH) Hacktoberfest Hack Day, themed around Halloween and powered by Open-Source AI (Gemini / Gemma APIs).
Whether you are a beginner looking to make your very first GitHub commit or a tech enthusiast wanting to build an AI-powered project, this interactive hack day is built for you!
📅 Updated Event Details
Date: 1 November 2026 (Halloween Special)
Timing: 09:00 AM – 01:00 PM IST (4-Hour Focused Online Hack Day)
Venue: COMPLETELY ONLINE (Google Meet link will be shared in the WhatsApp Group)
🚀 What Makes This Event Special?
In this single-day event, you will:
Learn & Demystify: Master Git & GitHub basics (Fork, Clone, Commit, and Pull Requests) from scratch.
Build & Innovate: Create lightweight open-source AI tools, Python scripts, or web utilities using modern AI models (Google Gemma, Gemini API).
Contribute & Ship: Raise your very first official Open-Source Pull Request (PR) live on GitHub and contribute to community projects.
Post-Hackathon Interactive Workshop & Live Quiz: Right after the winners are announced, we will host an exclusive interactive workshop followed by a live coding quiz!
🏆 Prizes & Rewards Breakdown
🎁 Top 6 Winners Track:
Top 6 Winners will receive the complete winner package: Official Winner Certificate + Arduino Hardware Kit + Exclusive T-Shirt + Sticker Pack! 🛠️👕📜✨
🧠 Post-Workshop Live Quiz Winners (2 Participants):
Right after the winner announcement, 2 participants will win rewards during our special workshop and live quiz:
🥇 Quiz Winner 1: Exclusive T-Shirt 👕
🥈 Quiz Winner 2: Arduino Hardware Kit 🛠️
✨ For All Participants & Attendees:
Official Digital Certificates: Every active participant will receive an official MLH & Hacktoberfest Digital Certificate.
Stickers: The remaining 40 active student participants will receive exclusive sticker packs!
📍 Important Note Regarding Reward Distribution
⚠️ Mandatory Physical Reward Ceremony:
All physical rewards (Arduino Kits, T-Shirts, and Sticker Packs) will be handed over to winners and quiz champions at a designated offline location.
Note: Group/individual photographs with winners while presenting the physical rewards are mandatory for event documentation and compliance. The exact offline meetup date and venue details will be announced during the online event.
⚠️ Important Guidelines & What To Prepare
AI TOOL for creating your project (claude, Antigravity)
Laptop & Stable Internet: Mandatory for building projects and streaming on Google Meet (Keep a mobile hotspot backup ready).
Pre-created GitHub Account: Make sure you have an active account ready at github.com.
Code of Conduct: All attendees must strictly follow the MLH Code of Conduct to maintain a safe and inclusive environment.
Team Formations: You can join solo or form teams of up to 4 members.
👥 Who Can Attend?
All College / University Students
Beginners in Tech & Coding who want a zero-to-hero GitHub & AI learning curve.
Come for the code, stay for the spooky fun, and win amazing rewards!

title: Hacktoberfest Hack Day x AI for Vizag
address:
Siripuram Junction
5th Floor, The Deck Building
Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh 530003
India
description:
AI for Vizag is hosting a Hacktoberfest Mini Hack Day — a hands-on build event for students, developers, designers, founders, and AI enthusiasts who want to explore open-source AI by actually building something.
Hacktoberfest is a global celebration of open source, and this mini hack day brings that spirit to Vizag with a focused theme: learning, building, and contributing through open-source AI tools, open-weight models, agents, and developer workflows.
This is not a lecture-only meetup. Participants will form teams, pick a prize track (Best Open-Source AI Project / Best Use of Gemma 4), build a working prototype, and demo it by the end of the day. Whether you are a beginner trying your first AI project or an experienced builder experimenting with agents and open-source tools, this event is designed to help you move from idea to working demo.
You can build AI agents, productivity tools, local problem-solving apps, developer utilities, student-focused tools, community solutions, or any useful AI-powered project using open-source or openly accessible technologies.
Make sure your project sticks to the prize track:
Best Open-Source AI Project -
https://www.mlh.com/events/hacktoberfest-hack-day-vizag-x-ai-for-vizag/challenges/01a0d987-0c41-12ea-13ac-5b85755dc2f3
Best Use of Gemma 4 -
https://www.mlh.com/events/hacktoberfest-hack-day-vizag-x-ai-for-vizag/challenges/01a03b87-be22-9180-5e2d-b3beeb66666d
Mentors will be available during the event to help teams refine ideas, unblock technical issues, and prepare their final demos.
Who can attend:
Students, working professionals, developers, designers, product managers, founders, and anyone interested in building with AI.
What to bring:
A laptop, charger, GitHub/GitLab account, internet backup if possible, and a willingness to build.
Team format:
Participants can join solo or as teams. Team formation support will be available at the venue.
By the end of the day, every team is expected to submit a working prototype, a short demo, and a project write-up.
Come build with the community. Vizag is not just watching the AI wave — Vizag is building it.

description:
Hacktoberfest Hack Day Muridke × AWS Student Builder Group
Build. Hack. Collaborate. Contribute.
Get ready for a hands-on Hack Day designed for students who want to experience what it feels like to build, collaborate, and solve real-world challenges as a team.
Hosted by AWS Student Builder Group — Punjab College Muridke as part of Hacktoberfest 2026, this beginner-friendly event brings students together for an afternoon of teamwork, problem-solving, open-source exploration, AI-powered building, and practical development.
You don't need to be an expert.
You just need a laptop, a willingness to learn, and a team ready to build.
What you'll experience
🧑‍💻 Team-based Hack Day challenges
🤖 Beginner-friendly AI & open-source building
🧩 Problem-solving and rapid prototyping
☁️ Exposure to modern cloud & developer tools
🔀 Git & GitHub collaboration
🏆 Challenge-based competition
🎁 Swags and prizes for selected winners
🏷️ Participation badges
🍕 Refreshments & community networking
Who can join?
University and college students are welcome.
Whether you're taking your first steps into development or already building projects, the challenges will be designed to give everyone a meaningful role within their team.
What to bring
Your laptop is mandatory.
Please come with your laptop charged and ready for hands-on activities.
Date: Sunday, November 1, 2026
Time: 10:00 AM – 3:00 PM
Venue: Mehak Royal Palace, Muridke
Registration is free.
Spots are limited, so register early and get ready to build something together.
